# Social signup and user accounts

Label: wayfinder:map

## Destination

An implementation-ready specification for managed social signup and user accounts in Cup, covering the auth SaaS choice, account ownership, initial free conversions, private account audiobooks, and coexistence with shared trial links on web and Android using Google sign-in. The map is complete when no decisions block implementation; application implementation is a separate effort.

## Notes

[Draft specification](spec.md) consolidates the agreed decisions and lists remaining gaps. It is not implementation-ready; provider setup and integration proofs remain pending.

Use the wayfinder, grilling, and domain-modeling skills for decision sessions; research sessions use research, and Markdown changes use write-markdown. Follow docs/agents/issue-tracker.md for this local Markdown tracker. Child tickets live in issues/; use their titles in conversation, claim before work, and query open unblocked children instead of keeping an open-ticket list here.

Confirmed scope and preferences from Patrick:

- Current scope, revised by Patrick on 2026-09-22: Google sign-in on web and Android. Android must use the native Google login flow, not browser authentication. Apple sign-in on every platform and the entire iOS app are deferred to a future task. This supersedes earlier platform/provider requirements in historical ticket comments and research.
- Use a managed SaaS; prefer a suitable Cloudflare offering. Prefer a usable free tier and predictable paid growth, without requiring free service.
- New accounts receive free conversions; the allowance decision below defines the agreed rules.
- Account-created audiobooks require their owner to sign in, including playback and downloads. Ownership must support future conversion history.
- Keep Android playback simple: measure the existing HTML player with a realistic long MP3 before deciding whether native playback is necessary. The native experiment is paused; background behavior and limits are tracked in the [media proof](issues/14-authenticated-media-proof.md).
- Remove the existing trial-grant history API access. Trial-created audiobooks retain individual link-based access; a shared trial link must not expose a discoverable history of other people's conversions.
- Signup may prevent returning to trial access. Trial credits need not transfer because new accounts receive their own allowance.
- This effort produces decisions and an implementation-ready specification, not application changes.

Current glossary calls the allowance unit a conversion slot and explicitly distinguishes grant credentials from user identity. The grant-session definition excludes shared-grant history access under the resolved access policy. Do not treat trial grants as people.

Research assets live alongside this map. No research branch is created without explicit approval, following the repository Git guardrail. Store research conclusions in their ticket and linked artifact; choosing the provider remains a human decision.

## Decisions so far

- [Which managed auth services fit Cup across web, Android, and iOS?](issues/01-auth-saas-research.md): No verified Cloudflare consumer-auth fit; Auth0 has an official Capacitor React path, Supabase has lower transparent MAU costs, and Clerk needs a Capacitor integration spike.

- [Which auth services support native Google on Android and native Apple on iOS through Capacitor?](issues/10-native-social-sso-research.md): Firebase and Supabase have the clearest existing native paths; Auth0 needs session glue, Clerk/Stytch custom integration, and standard Cognito user-pool federation does not qualify.

- [Which auth SaaS should Cup adopt?](issues/02-auth-provider-choice.md): Supabase manages identities and authentication sessions; Cup owns accounts, conversions, and allowances. Use hosted production Auth and local CLI/Docker development, with native integration still to validate.

- [How should accounts own conversions independently of trial grants?](issues/03-account-ownership.md): Stable Cup accounts stay separate from trial grants; signup/sign-in imports eligible installation-started trial results as independent copies with duplicated files, source relationships, and persistent account association.

- [What free allowance should a new account receive and how is it consumed?](issues/04-welcome-allowance.md): Three non-expiring welcome slots, reserved on start and spent on success; failures release slots, imports are free, deletion does not refund, and basic rate limits apply.

- [Can private-content requests be rejected immediately after session revocation?](issues/13-immediate-revocation-research.md): Fresh Supabase session checks can reject new requests after confirmed logout; hosted verification and authenticated media transport remain necessary.

- [How should private account audiobooks and shared trial links be authorized?](issues/05-access-and-trial-isolation.md): Owner-only account content, five-minute locally verified JWTs, current-session logout, and no shared trial history; authenticated media transport needs a compatibility proof.

- [How should signup, returning visits, and trial-to-account transitions behave?](issues/06-account-and-trial-journeys.md): URL-first authentication resumes submission, accounts take precedence over trials, and current trial-result continuity is preserved while all history listings are deferred.

- [What must Cup revoke when deleting an account authenticated through Apple or Google?](issues/16-account-deletion-research.md): Cup must handle Apple authorization revocation separately from Supabase identity deletion; token custody and native disconnect need integration proof.

- [How should account deletion and identity revocation work?](issues/09-account-deletion.md): Immediate access restriction, seven-day explicit recovery, background final deletion and provider revocation, notification emails, and a fresh allowance on later re-registration.

- [Which Cloudflare mechanism should durably execute trial-conversion copies?](issues/17-copy-execution-research.md): Workflows fits durable orchestration; Cup still needs persistent import identity, deadline enforcement, dispatch recovery, and protection against stale writes.

- [How should trial conversions be copied reliably into accounts?](issues/11-trial-conversion-copy.md): Dedicated Workflows copy a stable snapshot with persistent Cup state, eight-hour retry windows, manual partial cleanup, and independent exports.

- [How should Cloudflare persist accounts and safely provision their ownership?](issues/12-account-storage-and-provisioning.md): Per-account SQLite Durable Objects, an identity directory, append-only credit accounting, private import receipts, and durable dispatch preserve existing trial data.

- [Which managed email service should deliver account-deletion notifications?](issues/18-transactional-email-research.md): Cloudflare provides outbound sending and local simulation; ambiguous retries may duplicate mail, and Apple relay delivery still needs verification.

- [Can Cloudflare or Sentry SaaS enforce fourteen-day failure-telemetry retention?](issues/20-telemetry-retention-research.md): Workers Logs retains seven days maximum; Sentry Logs retains thirty days; provider selection needs a retention tradeoff or additional archive setup.

- [How should Terraform manage the existing signup infrastructure?](issues/21-terraform-adoption-research.md): GCP/Supabase have official providers; Resend domain management needs a vetted community provider; choose protected state storage before adoption.

- [Is the GCS Terraform state backend ready?](issues/22-terraform-state-bootstrap.md): Separate infrastructure project is billed through Cup Billing; private versioned GCS bucket exists in europe-west3, ready for Terraform initialization.

- [Is Terraform initialized with the existing bootstrap infrastructure adopted?](issues/23-terraform-initialization.md): Bootstrap project and bucket imported with a no-change plan; separate production backend initialized, awaiting application provider adoption.

- [Are the existing application services adopted into Terraform?](issues/24-application-terraform-adoption.md): GCP and Resend imported; replacement Supabase project created through Terraform with five-minute JWTs; full production plan reports no changes.

## Not yet specified

Further operational prerequisites may emerge from the concrete storage and authorization decisions; ticket them when specific.

## Out of scope

- Apple sign-in on all platforms and the iOS app, including Google on iOS, Apple provider setup/revocation, private-relay delivery, cross-provider linking, and iOS authentication/media proofs. See the [future-task handoff](deferred-apple-ios.md); these do not block the current Android/web Google scope.

- Account conversion-history UI and all imported-conversion listings. Imports are persisted under the account now; continuity for the currently open eligible trial conversion through sign-in remains in scope.
- Replacing conversion-based allowance with listening time, character counts, or another billing unit.
- Payments, money/payment accounting, checkout, subscriptions, and purchased top-ups. An append-only credit ledger is in scope; its design lives in the account-storage decision.
- Transferring trial credits to an account.
- Merging already-created accounts. Adding another provider and Google/Apple identity linking are deferred with Apple sign-in.
- Application implementation, deployment, and detailed visual design during map charting.

# What rollout and acceptance criteria make the account specification implementation-ready?

Type: grilling

Label: wayfinder:grilling

Status: claimed

Assignee: patricktree

Blocked by: 04, 05, 06, 08, 09, 11, 12, 14, 19

Map: [Social signup and user accounts](../map.md)

## Current scope — 2026-09-22

Patrick narrowed this effort to Google sign-in on Android and web. Apple sign-in on all platforms, the entire iOS app, cross-provider linking, Apple revocation and private-relay checks are deferred in the [future-task handoff](../deferred-apple-ios.md). Earlier comments describing them as launch requirements or blockers are superseded. All other account, allowance, trial-copy, privacy and deletion decisions remain applicable. Remaining Google/web proofs are not waived by this scope change.

## Question

Set rollout, existing-trial compatibility, migration, environment configuration, and acceptance-test requirements for the chosen account design across web and Android with Google sign-in. Identify any remaining provider setup or integration uncertainty requiring a research, prototype, or prerequisite task before implementation.

Resolve how the final spec is assembled at ../spec.md from the decision tickets without silently making outstanding product decisions. Acceptance must cover one-time free allowance, returning sign-in, concurrent/retried conversions, owner-only playback/downloads, trial-history isolation, trial-to-account transition, and native callbacks. This ticket plans implementation and validation; it does not implement or deploy the feature.

Set concrete launch rate-limit thresholds and enforcement for signup-triggered account provisioning and conversion attempts, following the [resolved allowance policy](04-welcome-allowance.md). Stronger person-level detection is deferred.

Include scheduled-deletion and completion emails from the [deletion decision](09-account-deletion.md). Specify delivery and retry handling, operational retention and cleanup completion criteria, provider revocation failure handling, and tests for restore/deadline races and re-registration during cleanup.

Make the [copy lifecycle](11-trial-conversion-copy.md) operationally concrete: set retry backoff within the eight-hour deadline, dispatch/source recheck intervals, per-file copy bounds, manual partial-cleanup procedure, and validation of interruption, stale execution, and deletion races. History UI remains deferred.

Patrick rejected a full prelaunch data reset: preserve existing grants, conversions, artifacts, and links. Existing trial conversions without recorded import evidence remain usable through their individual links but are not automatically imported into accounts. Plan compatible migration and in-flight workflow handling.

Apply the [storage decision](12-account-storage-and-provisioning.md): specify compatible owner-routing/schema migration for existing and in-flight trials; provisioning/deletion race tests; private receipt persistence and redaction; ledger invariants and reconstruction checks; and durable dispatch recovery. Pin implementation table/constraint definitions and state-transition contracts to these decisions before final handoff, without silently introducing new product policy.

## Comments

Patrick requested proceeding with independent rollout/acceptance decisions while access to the Apple Developer membership account is temporarily unavailable. Native-auth and authenticated-media dependencies remain intact; this ticket may be worked partially but cannot be resolved or the specification called implementation-ready until those proofs are complete.

Patrick chose a single rollout with minimum operational effort: Cup has no users yet and downtime is acceptable. Do not add staged rollout or internal enablement machinery solely for this feature. Existing data and links must still be preserved under the no-reset decision. Patrick rejected emergency controls; do not add provisioning/conversion/import pause switches.

Patrick confirmed automatic copy retry backoff starting at ten seconds, doubling after failures to a five-minute cap with jitter, within the absolute eight-hour window. Manual retry starts a new window under the resolved copy policy. Q3 remains open: explain missed-dispatch recovery and source-readiness fallback checks before selecting their timing/mechanism.

Patrick confirmed one-minute recovery checks for persisted jobs whose Workflow launch was missed, and durable one-minute polling while imports wait for source readiness. Do not add completion-notification machinery for that waiting path. Source waiting remains outside the eight-hour copy retry window. These are target check intervals, not hard recovery-latency guarantees during infrastructure outages.

Patrick confirmed configurable initial rate limits: ten newly provisioned Cup accounts per hour per IP, excluding returning sign-ins and retries for an existing account; ten conversion start requests per minute per account/trial grant and sixty per minute per IP, checked before expensive work. Idempotency still prevents duplicate conversions/charges.

For rate-limit rejection, preserve input and options, show a server-derived retry delay with a countdown, disable submission until it elapses, then re-enable without automatically submitting. For provisioning limits, explain that too many accounts were created from the network and retain the authenticated session while valid so retry does not require another provider sign-in. No credits are spent on rejected requests. No CAPTCHA or extra verification flow is added.

Patrick confirmed final-deletion failures keep access blocked and restoration disabled, with automatic retries using increasing delays capped at one hour. Flag cleanup incomplete after twenty-four hours for operator review while continuing retries. Notification failures do not delay deletion; retry delivery independently for up to twenty-four hours, then record failure for operator review. Send completion notification only after cleanup finishes.

Extend the existing operator CLI to inspect and retry failed jobs and preview/delete abandoned partial copies. No new admin dashboard. Manual cleanup previews exact files and refuses files belonging to an active copy; preserve import identity after partial cleanup.

Patrick confirmed automated acceptance coverage for provisioning, ledger invariants, authorization, import retries, deletion races and existing-trial compatibility, plus real-device Google/Apple authentication and private playback checks on Android/iOS and a web baseline. Patrick selected Sentry SaaS for observability. During setup, check whether supported fourteen-day Logs retention is available and configure it if possible; otherwise accept the standard thirty-day Logs retention without another approval. Record the actual policy used. This supersedes the previous strict fourteen-day requirement and pending provider choice. User email is permitted in deletion/notification failure logs. Keep email off longer-retained error events, global user context, spans, and other telemetry sinks unless their retention also meets the accepted policy. Diagnostic retention remains separate from notification payload retention and does not enable resend after payload purge. No Sentry project or retention configuration has been created or verified yet.

Patrick confirmed import evidence has no time-based expiry: retain the installation receipt and source-side hash while the original trial conversion exists; clearing installation storage may lose the local evidence. He also confirmed deletion and notification retry delays start at one minute, double with jitter, and cap at one hour. Honor provider retry instructions without extending the existing absolute twenty-three-hour email deadline. Copy retry timing remains unchanged.

Patrick did not accept removing all completed operational history; he wants to retain something after cleanup. The contents and lifetime of a minimal completed-deletion record remain open. This does not change the approved notification payload purge or Sentry telemetry retention.

Patrick accepted the proposed minimal completed-deletion receipt contents (attempt ID, former Cup account ID, request/deadline/completion timestamps, Cup/Supabase/Apple cleanup outcomes and notification outcomes), but proposed indefinite retention instead of ninety days and adding Supabase/Apple user identifiers. Retention and provider-identifier inclusion remain under discussion: these identifiers must be treated as pseudonymous personal data, not assumed anonymous. See [European Commission personal-data guidance](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/information-business-and-organisations/application-gdpr_en). No indefinite-retention policy has been finalized on the premise that the identifiers are non-personal.

Patrick confirmed ninety-day retention for the completed-deletion receipt, including former Cup account ID, Supabase user ID and Apple user identifier when applicable. Treat these as pseudonymous personal data. Retain deletion attempt ID, requested/recovery-deadline/completed timestamps, Cup cleanup/Supabase deletion/Apple revocation outcomes and notification outcomes. The ninety-day period starts once deletion and notification processing have both finished, including terminal notification failure or retry exhaustion; automatically purge the receipt afterward. This replaces the proposed indefinite retention. Receipt access is through the operator CLI; no email addresses, tokens or detailed error payloads belong in it. Sentry diagnostic retention and notification payload purge remain separate.

Patrick confirmed rolling rate-limit windows: sixty seconds for conversion starts and one hour for new account provisioning. Recovering an already accepted conversion bypasses the account/trial start limit but still counts toward the IP request limit. Rejected requests do not extend the cooldown. Thresholds remain ten starts/minute/account or trial grant, sixty start requests/minute/IP, and ten new Cup accounts/hour/IP. The proposed fifteen-second automatic provisioning retry window remains unconfirmed; Patrick requested an explanation of why provisioning can temporarily fail.

Patrick confirmed durable account provisioning through the directory Durable Object and its alarm. Persist pending setup and the stable Cup account ID before acknowledging acceptance; initialize the account and welcome grant idempotently, then activate. Attempt promptly and resume interrupted work without requiring an open client. The client checks progress and resumes that view after reopening; retrying a request that was never durably accepted remains necessary. This replaces the proposed browser-owned fifteen-second retry budget. Patrick delegated selection of this pattern elsewhere to implementation judgment.

Apply persisted job state plus alarms to small state-owned tasks: missed Workflow dispatch, deletion deadline scheduling, notification delivery retries and expiry of completed-deletion receipts. Keep conversion and trial-copy execution in Workflows. Deletion coordination must persist beyond account-data removal; its bounded cleanup steps may use alarms, while long-running work may use Workflows. These choices do not change retry deadlines, manual-only abandoned-copy cleanup, or account deletion semantics. Persist job progress, next-attempt times and absolute deadlines; use replay-safe effects and explicitly rearm alarms beyond built-in retry limits. One alarm schedules the earliest due job in each object. Do not delete the only coordinator before its remaining work or retention expiry completes.

Patrick approved adopting Terraform for supported Supabase, GCP and Resend configuration, importing existing resources rather than recreating them. Unsupported Google OAuth/Apple setup remains a documented manual prerequisite. Verify provider resource/import coverage, secret handling and protected state storage before any apply. Repository inspection found no existing Terraform configuration; terraform is installed locally. This approval establishes the configuration-management direction; no infrastructure migration or apply has been performed.

Patrick permits recreating the GCP and Supabase projects if simpler than import. This exception does not authorize a reset of existing Cup trial data or replacing the verified Resend setup. Terraform state backend selection remains pending after the adoption research.

Patrick selected a private Google Cloud Storage bucket in Europe for Terraform state, using the native gcs backend with state locking, object versioning and public access blocked. Keep it in a stable infrastructure project separate from the potentially replaceable cup-production project. Bootstrap the bucket before backend initialization. This supersedes the HCP recommendation; no HCP account is required. Exact bootstrap project/bucket and billing configuration remain to be established.

# Does Google sign-in work reliably on Android and web?

Type: prototype

Label: wayfinder:prototype

Status: claimed

Assignee: patricktree

Blocked by: 02, 15

Map: [Social signup and user accounts](../map.md)

## Current scope — 2026-09-22

Patrick narrowed this effort to Google sign-in on Android and web. Apple sign-in on all platforms, the entire iOS app, cross-provider linking, Apple revocation and private-relay checks are deferred in the [future-task handoff](../deferred-apple-ios.md). Earlier comments describing them as launch requirements or blockers are superseded. All other account, allowance, trial-copy, privacy and deletion decisions remain applicable. Remaining Google/web proofs are not waived by this scope change.

## Question

Use a focused throwaway prototype to validate native Google signup and returning login on Android without browser authentication, plus Google OAuth on web. Resolve web PKCE callback/session handling, cancellation, secure native storage, restart/refresh, logout, stable identity across devices and Worker token validation. Include Google disconnect/lifecycle behavior. Apple sign-in, iOS and cross-provider linking are deferred.

A vendor's React Native SDK or a configured Capacitor origin alone is not evidence of a working flow. Link the prototype and record observed behavior, limitations, and the resulting integration decision. If service configuration or credentials are missing, create a precise prerequisite task instead of pretending the flow was validated. This is a decision prototype, not production feature implementation.

Research context: [Managed authentication options for Cup](../auth-saas-research.md).

## Context

Patrick selected Supabase on 2026-09-18. Validate native provider credential acquisition followed by Supabase signInWithIdToken. Include a local Supabase CLI/Docker configuration where practical, with real Google provider setup and device-to-development-host connectivity. Local availability does not imply offline social sign-in. The resolved ownership decision assigns Supabase identities/sessions and Cup accounts/allowances to their respective services.

## Comments

Initial inspection identified missing local auth integration/configuration. The [provider and device setup prerequisite](15-native-auth-setup.md) tracks access needed for real execution. No native login has been demonstrated, and this proof remains unresolved. Use the agreed five-minute JWT policy and test native identity linking as well as sign-in.

The [deletion research](16-account-deletion-research.md) adds proof requirements: capture/exchange native Apple authorization codes, securely retain revocable provider credentials associated with the linked identity, verify web Apple credential custody separately, and test revocation and Google platform-specific disconnect. Cover linking Apple to an existing Google-created account. Supabase user deletion alone does not establish upstream revocation.

Prepared an isolated [Android Google prototype](../../../apps/mobile-app/prototype-auth/README.md) using Capacitor 8.5.1, Capawesome Google Sign-In 0.1.4 and Supabase JS 2.117.0. Installed plugin source uses Android CredentialManager/GetSignInWithGoogleOption. The prototype hashes a random nonce for Google and passes the raw nonce to Supabase, displays only safe result fields, and supports explicit refresh and local logout with in-memory sessions. No production app dependencies/native projects were changed. Android assembleDebug succeeded; APK signing verification matches the requested OAuth fingerprint. Native runtime execution remains pending Android client registration and an available device. adb lists no devices. This is a partial Android proof, not resolution of the full native-auth ticket; no login result is claimed.

## Android core proof result

On 2026-09-22 Patrick tested the prototype on a connected Pixel 10 Pro. Confirmed that Google sign-in opens a native sheet without a browser and that the Google ID token exchanges successfully for a Supabase session. Explicit Supabase session refresh succeeds. Local logout followed by another native sign-in returns the same Supabase user ID. Canceling the native sheet reports “Native login canceled.” These are user-observed runtime results, not conclusions from source inspection alone.

The core Android Credential Manager → Google ID token → Supabase session flow is validated with nonce checking enabled. Android OAuth registration uses the debug signing certificate, while the plugin uses the Web client ID as its audience. The full ticket remains claimed: secure session persistence/restart, Worker authorization, identity linking, iOS/Apple, remaining platform combinations and relevant lifecycle/deletion proofs are outstanding. The final test sequence ended signed out, followed by a canceled login. The prototype remains installed in place of the normal Cup debug app.

Extended the Android prototype with @aparajita/capacitor-secure-storage 8.0.0, an asynchronous Supabase storage adapter, and startup session restoration followed by server-side getUser validation. Inspected the installed Android source: AES/GCM encryption uses Android Keystore keys and stores ciphertext in private SharedPreferences; removal removes the preference and key. The client is only created on Android, preventing the plugin's plaintext web fallback. Automatic background refresh remains disabled to make expiration testing explicit. Generated manifest disables Android backup. Build passes; runtime restart/expiry/logout persistence observations are still pending. No production storage decision is inferred from build success.

Android restart proof passed on the Pixel 10 Pro: after Patrick signed in, the agent force-stopped com.cup_audio.app through ADB and relaunched it with a confirmed COLD launch. Patrick confirmed “Session restored after app startup and verified with Supabase,” the same user ID and no new sign-in prompt. This establishes restoration across process death using the secure-storage adapter. Restoration after access-token expiry and persistence removal after logout still require separate observations.

Android logout persistence proof passed: Patrick signed out, the agent force-stopped the app and confirmed a COLD relaunch, and Patrick confirmed “Ready. No stored session. Tap Sign in with Google.” The app stayed signed out across process restart. Restoration after access-token expiry remains untested; the successful earlier explicit refresh and unexpired restart tests do not substitute for that combined case.

Expired-token restart test: session created at 2026-09-22 14:43:43 UTC; app force-stopped before its five-minute access-token expiry and cold-launched after 14:48:43 UTC. Read-only Supabase session inspection confirms refreshed_at 14:49:42 UTC for that same session, establishing refresh after expiry on startup. First management lookup timed out; retry succeeded. Awaiting Patrick's confirmation of the restored-session screen without another login prompt.

Patrick confirmed the expired-token cold launch displayed “Session restored after app startup and verified with Supabase” without another sign-in prompt. Combined with the server-recorded refresh timestamp, the Android expired-token restart proof passes. Android now has observed native login, nonce-validated Supabase exchange, explicit refresh, stable identity on relogin, cancellation, encrypted session restoration across process death, logout persistence and refresh after expiry. This does not resolve the full cross-platform ticket: iOS/Apple, identity linking, Worker authorization and other listed lifecycle proofs remain outstanding.

Local Worker validation proof on 2026-09-22: the isolated prototype now includes an ES256 verifier restricted to the production Supabase issuer and authenticated audience, requiring subject, expiry, issued-at, session and role claims. Twelve tests passed in the Cloudflare workerd runtime using ephemeral fixture keys: valid token accepted; expired token, wrong issuer/audience/signature, missing expiry/subject/session, wrong role, future not-before, malformed token and absent token rejected. The real entry point uses Supabase remote JWKS, never fixture keys. The local Wrangler endpoint independently returned 401 for absent and malformed tokens. This establishes fixture behavior, not acceptance of a real phone session or Cup account authorization.

The Android prototype now has a “Verify session with local Worker” action that checks the real session identity and rejection of missing/invalid tokens through localhost forwarded over ADB. Updated APK builds successfully. The phone disconnected before installation, so the real-session check remains pending reconnection. No Worker was deployed and no production application auth was changed.

Real-session Worker proof passed on 2026-09-22: after reconnecting the Pixel 10 Pro, the updated APK was installed successfully and port 8788 forwarded over ADB to the local Wrangler Worker. Patrick confirmed the verification action displayed passed and HTTP 200. The action only reports passed when the real Supabase token receives 200 with the matching user identity and both invalid-token and missing-token requests receive 401. This validates Android → local Worker authentication using Supabase remote JWKS. It does not establish Cup account lifecycle checks or conversion ownership enforcement. The full ticket remains claimed for the outstanding cross-platform, linking and lifecycle requirements.

Web PKCE proof prepared on 2026-09-22 in the isolated prototype: separate web entry, explicit code exchange, immediate callback-parameter removal, browser-local session persistence, explicit refresh/current-session logout and same-origin proxy to the local Worker. Local page/module requests return 200 and the proxied unauthenticated Worker request returns 401. Terraform plan verified that only the exact localhost callback allowlist changes. Browser Google login and the subsequent session/lifecycle observations remain pending; the earlier implicit-flow baseline does not establish these results.

Patrick confirmed the web prototype displayed “PKCE exchange succeeded; identity verified” after Google login and that Worker verification reported passed on 2026-09-22. This establishes successful browser PKCE exchange, Supabase identity verification, and real-token acceptance with matching identity plus missing/invalid-token rejection through the local Worker proxy. Terraform applied the exact localhost callback allowlist successfully. Web reload restoration, explicit refresh, logout persistence and expired-token restoration remain separate pending observations.

Patrick confirmed web reload displayed “Stored session restored and verified” with the same user ID and no Google prompt, and explicit refresh displayed “Refresh succeeded.” Browser session restoration and explicit refresh pass. Logout persistence and restoration after access-token expiry remain pending; these checks do not substitute for those observations.

Patrick confirmed that web logout followed by reload displayed “Ready; no stored session” with session-action buttons disabled. Web logout persistence passes. Restoration after the five-minute access-token expiry remains pending; automatic background refresh is disabled in this prototype so this can be tested by leaving a newly signed-in session idle until its displayed expiresAt has passed and then reloading.

Patrick confirmed the web expired-token test worked: after signing in and leaving the page idle for six minutes without explicit refresh, reload restored and verified the session without another Google prompt, and Worker verification passed. Automatic background refresh was disabled. This is user-observed evidence of refresh on restoration after the five-minute access-token lifetime, rather than an independently inspected server timestamp. The core web session proof now passes PKCE login, identity verification, Worker validation, reload persistence, explicit refresh, logout persistence and expired-token restoration. This does not establish Google disconnect/deletion behavior, local OSS Supabase setup, cancellation/retry, or authenticated media transport; the broader proof ticket remains claimed.

# How should authenticated playback and downloads work across web and Capacitor?

Type: prototype

Label: wayfinder:prototype

Status: claimed

Assignee: patricktree

Blocked by: 05, 08

Map: [Social signup and user accounts](../map.md)

## Current scope — 2026-09-22

Patrick narrowed this effort to Google sign-in on Android and web. Apple sign-in on all platforms, the entire iOS app, cross-provider linking, Apple revocation and private-relay checks are deferred in the [future-task handoff](../deferred-apple-ios.md). Earlier comments describing them as launch requirements or blockers are superseded. All other account, allowance, trial-copy, privacy and deletion decisions remain applicable. Remaining Google/web proofs are not waived by this scope change.

## Question

Use a focused throwaway prototype to select credential transport for private HTML audio, captions, MP3 and EPUB downloads on web and Android. Existing anonymous media elements and direct links do not establish authenticated access. Demonstrate owner-only requests, seeking and range responses, HEAD/conditional responses, five-minute token expiry and refresh during playback, foreground/background transitions, logout cleanup, and generic denial to non-owners. Check cookies/CORS or alternative authenticated transport against real Capacitor behavior; do not substitute a transferable signed media URL for owner authentication. Verify private responses and storage cannot bypass authorization through caching or direct URLs.

Record observed device/browser evidence and agree the resulting transport with Patrick. Create precise prerequisite tasks for unavailable setup or devices. This is a decision prototype, not production implementation.

Resolve the playback transition from an original trial result to its private account copy with Patrick, as delegated by the trial-copy decision. Preserve access through signup, waiting, copying, and copy failure. Do not assume an automatic mid-playback switch; demonstrate the selected behavior on actual media transports.

## Comments

Starting a partial media proof after the core Android/web session checks passed. The broader auth ticket remains open for remaining Google lifecycle/local-development checks; this media work does not imply those are resolved. First test same-origin web cookie transport, then independently assess Android origin/cookie behavior.

Prepared a first web-only cookie transport proof in the [isolated prototype](../../../apps/mobile-app/prototype-auth/README.md). A bearer-authenticated endpoint sets an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie containing the same short-lived JWT; the media route verifies it and a fixed prototype owner before serving a synthetic eight-minute WAV. Every response is private/no-store. Production must use Secure cookies and appropriate origin/path/CSRF design; the HTTP localhost cookie is only a proof. No public storage URL or token-bearing media URL is used. A foreground timer updates the cookie from the Supabase session every thirty seconds while this media proof is loaded; logout pauses/unloads audio and clears the cookie. This is not yet an agreed production transport.

Local workerd tests pass for anonymous denial, non-owner 404, expired-token denial, authenticated byte ranges, invalid ranges, anonymous conditional-request denial, owner/anonymous HEAD and cookie issuance, alongside all twelve JWT tests. The fixture owner is Patrick's existing Supabase subject; tests sign ephemeral tokens with a separate fixture key. No new real account or private audio was created. Runtime browser playback/seeking/download/logout observations remain pending. Android cross-origin cookie behavior, background/expiry recovery, captions, MP3/EPUB, full conditional semantics and trial-copy player transition remain unproven. Current synthetic WAV proof does not resolve this ticket.

Sources: [HTML media credential modes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLMediaElement/crossOrigin), [Capacitor native cookies](https://github.com/ionic-team/capacitor/blob/main/core/cookies.md). Cup currently uses an anonymous HTML audio element and direct download links; this proof investigates how those requests can carry owner credentials without a transferable signed media URL.

Patrick confirmed all initial web media observations: the synthetic WAV played with the expected beeps, seeking forward/backward resumed playback, the authenticated WAV download succeeded, logout stopped playback, and another download attempt after logout failed. This validates the initial same-origin browser cookie transport and visible logout cleanup for this fixture. It does not yet prove renewal across access-token expiry, background recovery, Android transport, captions or MP3/EPUB behavior. In particular, buffered playback is not evidence that a fresh request after expiry was authorized.

Patrick confirmed the foreground expiry test worked: after signing in, loading/playing media and keeping the tab in the foreground for six minutes, another WAV download succeeded and the displayed media-session expiresAt advanced. This is user-observed evidence of foreground session/cookie renewal and a fresh authenticated media request after the original five-minute token lifetime. It does not establish behavior while browser timers are suspended, Android cookie transport, or recovery from a failed refresh. The media proof remains claimed.

On 2026-09-23 prepared the Android cross-origin media experiment: an additional local HTTPS Worker on port 8789, exact credentialed CORS for the Capacitor origin <https://localhost>, HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=None media cookies and a debug-only Android trust anchor for the locally generated certificate. TLS validation remains enabled, the private key stays in ignored host storage, and no Worker is deployed. Android UI uses WebView fetch with credentials and a credentialed audio element; this intentionally tests WebView cookie/media behavior rather than inferring it from CapacitorHttp. Logout pauses/unloads audio and clears the endpoint cookie. The download button verifies full WAV transfer, not saving to Android Downloads.

APK build and the existing twenty-one Worker checks pass; a TLS-verified unauthenticated request to the new endpoint returns 401. Pixel is absent from ADB, so installation and device observations remain pending reconnection. Build success and host-side checks do not establish Android cookie acceptance, playback, seeking or download transfer. HTTPS setup references are in the prototype README.

On 2026-09-23 the Pixel 10 Pro reconnected; the updated APK installed successfully, ADB forwarded ports 8789/8788, and the app cold-launched. Patrick confirmed all four Android media checks: credentialed audio played, seeking forward/backward resumed playback, full authenticated WAV transfer returned 200 with 7680044 bytes and passed, and logout stopped playback followed by a transfer returning 401. This establishes initial cross-origin WebView cookie transport with HTTPS and visible logout cleanup on the tested device. It does not establish Android Downloads saving, foreground renewal after expiry, background behavior, captions or MP3/EPUB compatibility. The broader media proof remains claimed.

Patrick confirmed the Android foreground expiry test on 2026-09-23: after signing in, loading/playing private audio and keeping the app foregrounded with the screen awake for six minutes, authenticated download transfer still reported passed and the media expiresAt advanced. This is user-observed evidence of foreground Supabase session/media-cookie renewal and a fresh authenticated request after the original five-minute token expired. Android background/screen-lock behavior and recovery after suspended timers remain unproven, as do actual Downloads saving, MP3/EPUB and captions.

Android background test failed: Patrick observed 401 for the first download transfer after locking the phone for six minutes. Whether playback continued throughout is unknown. Expired media authorization after suspended foreground renewal is the working explanation; no server-side expiry trace was captured for that request.

Updated the prototype with Capacitor App 8.1.1 foreground-state handling. It stops the foreground timer in the background, renews session/media-cookie authorization on resume, shares concurrent renewal work, and makes authenticated transfer await renewal when media is loaded. Failed renewal pauses playback and reports retry/sign-in guidance. Logout disables renewal and drains outstanding renewal before clearing the cookie. A temporary Node harness exercising the actual module with mocked lifecycle/network boundaries passed resume plus immediate transfer ordering and logout during renewal; this checks coordination, not real Android behavior. APK build passes. The six-minute lock/unlock device retest is still required, and uninterrupted background playback remains unknown.

Patrick confirmed the updated Android six-minute lock/unlock retest worked: after unlocking, an immediate authenticated transfer returned 200/passed without manually reloading audio. This validates post-resume authorization recovery on the tested Pixel, with transfer waiting for session/media-cookie renewal. The earlier post-unlock 401 is resolved for this tested path. Uninterrupted playback throughout screen lock and automatic recovery of a failed HTML audio resource remain unverified; transfer recovery does not establish either behavior.

Extended the local proof with a synthetic thirty-second MP3, three timed WebVTT cues and a minimal EPUB 3 test book. Assets are embedded only in the authenticated Worker; owner authorization precedes format/range responses. Added web/native format players with a visible caption-text display driven by track cues. Android has a prototype-only MediaStore Downloads plugin for small authenticated MP3/EPUB files, using pending insertion then publication, without storage permissions on Android 10+. JavaScript fetches the authorized file before passing its bytes to the native saver; whole-file buffering/base64 is intentionally limited to these small fixtures and is not a large-audiobook download design.

Existing Worker checks and additional MP3/VTT/EPUB owner/non-owner/anonymous checks plus MP3 range checks pass. ffprobe confirms thirty-second MP3 duration and unzip verifies EPUB archive integrity; EPUB-reader rendering remains unverified. Android APK builds successfully. Runtime format playback/captions, actual file saving/opening and denial after logout remain pending user observations. Existing external downloads should remain usable after logout by the agreed policy.

Patrick confirmed the Android MP3/captions/EPUB checklist: MP3 playback and seeking worked, caption text changed at the expected intervals, both test files appeared in Downloads and the opening check was confirmed, logout cleared playback/captions and blocked new saves while previously saved files remained. The response did not separately identify browser observations, so the corresponding web format checks remain pending. These results validate the small-fixture Android path; they do not establish large-file streaming, uninterrupted background playback or the trial-copy transition.

Patrick clarified that the same MP3/captions/EPUB checklist was also run successfully in the web prototype. Web MP3 playback/seeking, timed caption display, MP3/EPUB downloads/opening, logout clearing playback/captions and denial of new saves are therefore user-confirmed as well. Existing saved files remain usable. Both tested platforms now pass the small-fixture format/export checks; large-file transfer strategy, uninterrupted background playback, failed-player recovery and trial-copy transition remain unresolved.

Added an Android background observer to the eight-minute WAV player: arm while playing, capture monotonic elapsed time and media position on background/return, and report pause/playing/waiting/stalled/ended/error/seeking events. The first bounded observation is ninety seconds, distinct from the five-minute authentication-expiry tests. Position progress and WebView-delivered events are evidence of player behavior, not guaranteed continuous audible output or fresh authorized network traffic. Buffered content and suspended event delivery limit the observation. Device results remain pending.

Android recommends a native media playback service for reliable background playback; the current proof has no such service. Evaluate a native player and background credential-refresh ownership before committing to production background streaming. [Android Media3 guide](https://developer.android.com/media/implement/playback-app), [Capawesome Audio Player](https://capawesome.io/docs/sdks/capacitor/audio-player/). No paid plugin was acquired or production architecture selected. The observer APK builds successfully.

Patrick reported the Android background observation: elapsedSeconds 256, playbackProgressSeconds 256, pausedOnReturn false (clarified after the initial value was mistyped). The player advanced in line with elapsed time and remained playing on return on this Pixel. No event-list result was supplied. This supports continued playback during the observed lock period but does not prove uninterrupted audible output, new authenticated requests while backgrounded, five-minute-expiry renewal, or behavior under memory pressure. The observation lasted less than the configured access-token lifetime, and buffered content may explain continued playback.

Background streaming design boundary: inspection confirms the prototype clears its renewal timer when Android backgrounds the activity. Its only renewal paths are foreground timer, app resume and foreground user actions. Therefore it has no mechanism to refresh media credentials during a suspended WebView session; another long buffered-playback observation cannot establish fresh-request authorization after expiry. Expired-token rejection is already covered by Worker tests. No additional six-minute user test is requested for that unchanged mechanism.

For reliable background streaming, the candidate design is a native media playback service with native-side session refresh and authenticated media requests, independent of the WebView timer. Refresh-token rotation must have one coordinated owner across native playback and the UI; independently refreshing copied tokens from both sides is not an acceptable shortcut. A generic native-player plugin does not itself prove Supabase refresh integration. Android's recommended MediaSessionService keeps playback separate from the activity: [official guide](https://developer.android.com/media/media3/session/background-playback). This is a proposed direction, not a selected or validated implementation. Product scope choice remains: include reliable background streaming in the current release, or explicitly defer that guarantee and retain tested foreground/resume behavior. No JWT lifetime extension or public/signed media URL is proposed.

Patrick agreed to keep reliable screen-locked Android streaming in the current release and pursue native Android background playback with coordinated session refresh. This is a requirement and design direction, not a completed proof or selection of a specific plugin. The next prototype must demonstrate a fresh authenticated media request after access-token expiry while the screen remains locked, with playback and refresh independent of suspended WebView JavaScript. Native playback and the UI must share one coordinated refresh owner so rotation cannot race. Preserve five-minute JWTs, owner/lifecycle checks and logout cleanup. Also cover refresh failure with recoverable playback position. The successful HTML-player tests remain evidence for foreground/web transport, not fulfillment of this native background requirement.

Prepared a native Media3 1.11.1 MediaSessionService prototype with a ten-minute playlist of thirty-second synthetic MP3 items and ten-second maximum target buffering. Native request resolution supplies the current bearer token, serializes refresh under one native lock and refreshes near expiry without WebView JavaScript. The local Android Worker applies the existing JWT/owner checks to native bearer requests. Transfer-start instrumentation counts accepted native requests while the screen is noninteractive after the original token expiry; the report also exposes refresh count, playback position and a sanitized failure field. This tests fresh media access rather than only buffered position progress.

The bounded proof transfers refresh ownership to native: it drains/stops HTML-media renewal, makes other WebView controls inert and keeps Supabase automatic refresh disabled. Stop halts playback, waits for native refresh to finish and returns the latest tokens to Supabase secure storage without displaying them. Native-owned credentials are memory-only in this prototype; process-death recovery, seamless activity recreation, durable native credential custody, concurrent native/JS recovery and full logout/failure UX are not production-ready. Do not treat the temporary handoff as the final session architecture. APK build and existing Worker authorization/format tests pass; locked-expiry native runtime evidence remains pending. No production app or deployed Worker was changed.

Native startup initially failed for Patrick even after sign-out/sign-in. Inspection found the bridge used PluginCall.getLong for expires_at; the installed Capacitor implementation accepts only Java Long, while the current epoch-second value is represented as Integer. Changed the expiry boundary to accept Number.longValue. A standalone Java check reproduced rejection of the integer by the old accessor logic and verified the corrected conversion for Integer and Long timestamps. Added safe startup-stage/error-code reporting and disabled duplicate Start clicks. APK rebuild passes; startup/device retest remains required. No successful native background proof is claimed from this fix alone.

Patrick chose the simpler next step: pause the native-player experiment and measure the existing HTML player with one realistic long MP3 before deciding whether replacement is necessary. This supersedes treating native playback as an already-selected implementation direction; reliable background behavior remains the desired outcome, with limits to be documented from evidence. The earlier manual post-unlock download 401 did not demonstrate an audio-player request failing while locked.

Prepared a single 45-minute synthetic mono MP3 at Cup's actual 24 kHz/128 kbps encoding (43,201,196 bytes). It is stored in local R2 emulation only, served with normal ranges and owner checks, without forced segments, reconnects or throttling. A bounded in-memory request report records timestamps, methods, ranges and statuses, never credentials. The dedicated HTML player has no background renewal; reading its request report after unlock renews authorization for the report without reloading audio. Native controls are hidden for this run and no native playback service was running before reinstall. Build, fixture metadata checks and a focused auth-before-storage/range/report harness pass. Device playback/request observations remain pending; fast USB/local networking remains a limitation of this experiment.

# How should authenticated playback and downloads work across web and Capacitor?

Type: prototype

Label: wayfinder:prototype

Status: claimed

Assignee: patricktree

Blocked by: 05, 08

Map: [Social signup and user accounts](../map.md)

## Current scope — 2026-09-22

Patrick narrowed this effort to Google sign-in on Android and web. Apple sign-in on all platforms, the entire iOS app, cross-provider linking, Apple revocation and private-relay checks are deferred in the [future-task handoff](../deferred-apple-ios.md). Earlier comments describing them as launch requirements or blockers are superseded. All other account, allowance, trial-copy, privacy and deletion decisions remain applicable. Remaining Google/web proofs are not waived by this scope change.

## Question

Use a focused throwaway prototype to select credential transport for private HTML audio, captions, MP3 and EPUB downloads on web and Android. Existing anonymous media elements and direct links do not establish authenticated access. Demonstrate owner-only requests, seeking and range responses, HEAD/conditional responses, five-minute token expiry and refresh during playback, foreground/background transitions, logout cleanup, and generic denial to non-owners. Check cookies/CORS or alternative authenticated transport against real Capacitor behavior; do not substitute a transferable signed media URL for owner authentication. Verify private responses and storage cannot bypass authorization through caching or direct URLs.

Record observed device/browser evidence and agree the resulting transport with Patrick. Create precise prerequisite tasks for unavailable setup or devices. This is a decision prototype, not production implementation.

Resolve the playback transition from an original trial result to its private account copy with Patrick, as delegated by the trial-copy decision. Preserve access through signup, waiting, copying, and copy failure. Do not assume an automatic mid-playback switch; demonstrate the selected behavior on actual media transports.

## Comments

Starting a partial media proof after the core Android/web session checks passed. The broader auth ticket remains open for remaining Google lifecycle/local-development checks; this media work does not imply those are resolved. First test same-origin web cookie transport, then independently assess Android origin/cookie behavior.

Prepared a first web-only cookie transport proof in the [isolated prototype](../../../apps/mobile-app/prototype-auth/README.md). A bearer-authenticated endpoint sets an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie containing the same short-lived JWT; the media route verifies it and a fixed prototype owner before serving a synthetic eight-minute WAV. Every response is private/no-store. Production must use Secure cookies and appropriate origin/path/CSRF design; the HTTP localhost cookie is only a proof. No public storage URL or token-bearing media URL is used. A foreground timer updates the cookie from the Supabase session every thirty seconds while this media proof is loaded; logout pauses/unloads audio and clears the cookie. This is not yet an agreed production transport.

Local workerd tests pass for anonymous denial, non-owner 404, expired-token denial, authenticated byte ranges, invalid ranges, anonymous conditional-request denial, owner/anonymous HEAD and cookie issuance, alongside all twelve JWT tests. The fixture owner is Patrick's existing Supabase subject; tests sign ephemeral tokens with a separate fixture key. No new real account or private audio was created. Runtime browser playback/seeking/download/logout observations remain pending. Android cross-origin cookie behavior, background/expiry recovery, captions, MP3/EPUB, full conditional semantics and trial-copy player transition remain unproven. Current synthetic WAV proof does not resolve this ticket.

Sources: [HTML media credential modes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLMediaElement/crossOrigin), [Capacitor native cookies](https://github.com/ionic-team/capacitor/blob/main/core/cookies.md). Cup currently uses an anonymous HTML audio element and direct download links; this proof investigates how those requests can carry owner credentials without a transferable signed media URL.

Patrick confirmed all initial web media observations: the synthetic WAV played with the expected beeps, seeking forward/backward resumed playback, the authenticated WAV download succeeded, logout stopped playback, and another download attempt after logout failed. This validates the initial same-origin browser cookie transport and visible logout cleanup for this fixture. It does not yet prove renewal across access-token expiry, background recovery, Android transport, captions or MP3/EPUB behavior. In particular, buffered playback is not evidence that a fresh request after expiry was authorized.

Patrick confirmed the foreground expiry test worked: after signing in, loading/playing media and keeping the tab in the foreground for six minutes, another WAV download succeeded and the displayed media-session expiresAt advanced. This is user-observed evidence of foreground session/cookie renewal and a fresh authenticated media request after the original five-minute token lifetime. Android UI uses WebView fetch with credentials and a credentialed audio element; this intentionally tests WebView cookie/media behavior rather than inferring it from CapacitorHttp. Logout pauses/unloads audio and clears the endpoint cookie. The download button verifies full WAV transfer, not saving to Android Downloads.

Label: wayfinder:map

## Destination

An implementation-ready specification for managed social signup and user accounts in Cup, covering the auth SaaS choice, account ownership, initial free conversions, private account audiobooks, and coexistence with shared trial links on web and Android using Google sign-in. The map is complete when no decisions block implementation; application implementation is a separate effort.

## Notes

[Draft specification](spec.md) consolidates the agreed decisions and lists remaining gaps. It is not implementation-ready; provider setup and integration proofs remain pending.

Use the wayfinder, grilling, and domain-modeling skills for decision sessions; research sessions use research, and Markdown changes use write-markdown. Follow docs/agents/issue-tracker.md for this local Markdown tracker. Child tickets live in issues/; use their titles in conversation, claim before work, and query open unblocked children instead of keeping an open-ticket list here.

Confirmed scope and preferences from Patrick:

- Current scope, revised by Patrick on 2026-09-22: Google sign-in on web and Android. Android must use the native Google login flow, not browser authentication. Apple sign-in on every platform and the entire iOS app are deferred to a future task. This supersedes earlier platform/provider requirements in historical ticket comments and research.
- Use a managed SaaS; prefer a suitable Cloudflare offering. Prefer a usable free tier and predictable paid growth, without requiring free service.
- New accounts receive free conversions; the allowance decision below defines the agreed rules.
- Account-created audiobooks require their owner to sign in, including playback and downloads. Ownership must support future conversion history.
- Keep Android playback simple: measure the existing HTML player with a realistic long MP3 before deciding whether native playback is necessary. The native experiment is paused; background behavior and limits are tracked in the [media proof](issues/14-authenticated-media-proof.md).
- Remove the existing trial-grant history API access. Trial-created audiobooks retain individual link-based access; a shared trial link must not expose a discoverable history of other people's conversions.
- Signup may prevent returning to trial access. Trial credits need not transfer because new accounts receive their own allowance.
- This effort produces decisions and an implementation-ready specification, not application changes.

Current glossary calls the allowance unit a conversion slot and explicitly distinguishes grant credentials from user identity. The grant-session definition excludes shared-grant history access under the resolved access policy. Do not treat trial grants as people.

Research assets live alongside this map. No research branch is created without explicit approval, following the repository Git guardrail. Store research conclusions in their ticket and linked artifact; choosing the provider remains a human decision.

## Decisions so far

- [Which managed auth services fit Cup across web, Android, and iOS?](issues/01-auth-saas-research.md): No verified Cloudflare consumer-auth fit; Auth0 has an official Capacitor React path, Supabase has lower transparent MAU costs, and Clerk needs a Capacitor integration spike.

- [Which auth services support native Google on Android and native Apple on iOS through Capacitor?](issues/10-native-social-sso-research.md): Firebase and Supabase have the clearest existing native paths; Auth0 needs session glue, Clerk/Stytch custom integration, and standard Cognito user-pool federation does not qualify.

- [Which auth SaaS should Cup adopt?](issues/02-auth-provider-choice.md): Supabase manages identities and authentication sessions; Cup owns accounts, conversions, and allowances. Use hosted production Auth and local CLI/Docker development, with native integration still to validate.

- [How should accounts own conversions independently of trial grants?](issues/03-account-ownership.md): Stable Cup accounts stay separate from trial grants; signup/sign-in imports eligible installation-started trial results as independent copies with duplicated files, source relationships, and persistent account association.

- [What free allowance should a new account receive and how is it consumed?](issues/04-welcome-allowance.md): Three non-expiring welcome slots, reserved on start and spent on success; failures release slots, imports are free, deletion does not refund, and basic rate limits apply.

- [Can private-content requests be rejected immediately after session revocation?](issues/13-immediate-revocation-research.md): Fresh Supabase session checks can reject new requests after confirmed logout; hosted verification and authenticated media transport remain necessary.

- [How should private account audiobooks and shared trial links be authorized?](issues/05-access-and-trial-isolation.md): Owner-only account content, five-minute locally verified JWTs, current-session logout, and no shared trial history; authenticated media transport needs a compatibility proof.

- [How should signup, returning visits, and trial-to-account transitions behave?](issues/06-account-and-trial-journeys.md): URL-first authentication resumes submission, accounts take precedence over trials, and current trial-result continuity is preserved while all history listings are deferred.

- [What must Cup revoke when deleting an account authenticated through Apple or Google?](issues/16-account-deletion-research.md): Cup must handle Apple authorization revocation separately from Supabase identity deletion; token custody and native disconnect need integration proof.

- [How should account deletion and identity revocation work?](issues/09-account-deletion.md): Immediate access restriction, seven-day explicit recovery, background final deletion and provider revocation, notification emails, and a fresh allowance on later re-registration.

- [Which Cloudflare mechanism should durably execute trial-conversion copies?](issues/17-copy-execution-research.md): Workflows fits durable orchestration; Cup still needs persistent import identity, deadline enforcement, dispatch recovery, and protection against stale writes.

- [How should trial conversions be copied reliably into accounts?](issues/11-trial-conversion-copy.md): Dedicated Workflows copy a stable snapshot with persistent Cup state, eight-hour retry windows, manual partial cleanup, and independent exports.

- [How should Cloudflare persist accounts and safely provision their ownership?](issues/12-account-storage-and-provisioning.md): Per-account SQLite Durable Objects, an identity directory, append-only credit accounting, private import receipts, and durable dispatch preserve existing trial data.

- [Which managed email service should deliver account-deletion notifications?](issues/18-transactional-email-research.md): Cloudflare provides outbound sending and local simulation; ambiguous retries may duplicate mail, and Apple relay delivery still needs verification.

- [Can Cloudflare or Sentry SaaS enforce fourteen-day failure-telemetry retention?](issues/20-telemetry-retention-research.md): Workers Logs retains seven days maximum; Sentry Logs retains thirty days; provider selection needs a retention tradeoff or additional archive setup.

- [How should Terraform manage the existing signup infrastructure?](issues/21-terraform-adoption-research.md): GCP/Supabase have official providers; Resend domain management needs a vetted community provider; choose protected state storage before adoption.

- [Is the GCS Terraform state backend ready?](issues/22-terraform-state-bootstrap.md): Separate infrastructure project is billed through Cup Billing; private versioned GCS bucket exists in europe-west3, ready for Terraform initialization.

- [Is Terraform initialized with the existing bootstrap infrastructure adopted?](issues/23-terraform-initialization.md): Bootstrap project and bucket imported with a no-change plan; separate production backend initialized, awaiting application provider adoption.

- [Are the existing application services adopted into Terraform?](issues/24-application-terraform-adoption.md): GCP and Resend imported; replacement Supabase project created through Terraform with five-minute JWTs; full production plan reports no changes.

## Not yet specified

Further operational prerequisites may emerge from the concrete storage and authorization decisions; ticket them when specific.

## Out of scope

- Apple sign-in on all platforms and the iOS app, including Google on iOS, Apple provider setup/revocation, private-relay delivery, cross-provider linking, and iOS authentication/media proofs. See the [future-task handoff](deferred-apple-ios.md); these do not block the current Android/web Google scope.

- Account conversion-history UI and all imported-conversion listings. Imports are persisted under the account now; continuity for the currently open eligible trial conversion through sign-in remains in scope.
- Replacing conversion-based allowance with listening time, character counts, or another billing unit.
- Payments, money/payment accounting, checkout, subscriptions, and purchased top-ups. An append-only credit ledger is in scope; its design lives in the account-storage decision.
- Transferring trial credits to an account.
- Merging already-created accounts. Adding another provider and Google/Apple identity linking are deferred with Apple sign-in.
- Application implementation, deployment, and detailed visual design during map charting.

Type: prototype

Label: wayfinder:prototype

Status: claimed

Assignee: patricktree

Blocked by: 05, 08

Map: [Social signup and user accounts](../map.md)

## Current scope — 2026-09-22

Patrick narrowed this effort to Google sign-in on Android and web. Apple sign-in on all platforms, the entire iOS app, cross-provider linking, Apple revocation and private-relay checks are deferred in the [future-task handoff](../deferred-apple-ios.md). Earlier comments describing them as launch requirements or blockers are superseded. All other account, allowance, trial-copy, privacy and deletion decisions remain applicable. Remaining Google/web proofs are not waived by this scope change.

## Question

Use a focused throwaway prototype to select credential transport for private HTML audio, captions, MP3 and EPUB downloads on web and Android. Existing anonymous media elements and direct links do not establish authenticated access. Demonstrate owner-only requests, seeking and range responses, HEAD/conditional responses, five-minute token expiry and refresh during playback, foreground/background transitions, logout cleanup, and generic denial to non-owners. Check cookies/CORS or alternative authenticated transport against real Capacitor behavior; do not substitute a transferable signed media URL for owner authentication. Verify private responses and storage cannot bypass authorization through caching or direct URLs.

Record observed device/browser evidence and agree the resulting transport with Patrick. Create precise prerequisite tasks for unavailable setup or devices. This is a decision prototype, not production implementation.

Resolve the playback transition from an original trial result to its private account copy with Patrick, as delegated by the trial-copy decision. Preserve access through signup, waiting, copying, and copy failure. Do not assume an automatic mid-playback switch; demonstrate the selected behavior on actual media transports.

## Comments

Starting a partial media proof after the core Android/web session checks passed. The broader auth ticket remains open for remaining Google lifecycle/local-development checks; this media work does not imply those are resolved. First test same-origin web cookie transport, then independently assess Android origin/cookie behavior.

Prepared a first web-only cookie transport proof in the [isolated prototype](../../../apps/mobile-app/prototype-auth/README.md). A bearer-authenticated endpoint sets an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie containing the same short-lived JWT; the media route verifies it and a fixed prototype owner before serving a synthetic eight-minute WAV. Every response is private/no-store. Production must use Secure cookies and appropriate origin/path/CSRF design; the HTTP localhost cookie is only a proof. No public storage URL or token-bearing media URL is used. A foreground timer updates the cookie from the Supabase session every thirty seconds while this media proof is loaded; logout pauses/unloads audio and clears the cookie. This is not yet an agreed production transport.

Local workerd tests pass for anonymous denial, non-owner 404, expired-token denial, authenticated byte ranges, invalid ranges, anonymous conditional-request denial, owner/anonymous HEAD and cookie issuance, alongside all twelve JWT tests. The fixture owner is Patrick's existing Supabase subject; tests sign ephemeral tokens with a separate fixture key. No new real account or private audio was created. Runtime browser playback/seeking/download/logout observations remain pending. Android cross-origin cookie behavior, background/expiry recovery, captions, MP3/EPUB, full conditional semantics and trial-copy player transition remain unproven. Current synthetic WAV proof does not resolve this ticket.

Sources: [HTML media credential modes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLMediaElement/crossOrigin), [Capacitor native cookies](https://github.com/ionic-team/capacitor/blob/main/core/cookies.md). Cup currently uses an anonymous HTML audio element and direct download links; this proof investigates how those requests can carry owner credentials without a transferable signed media URL.

Patrick confirmed all initial web media observations: the synthetic WAV played with the expected beeps, seeking forward/backward resumed playback, the authenticated WAV download succeeded, logout stopped playback, and another download attempt after logout failed. This validates the initial same-origin browser cookie transport and visible logout cleanup for this fixture. It does not yet prove renewal across access-token expiry, background recovery, Android transport, captions or MP3/EPUB behavior. In particular, buffered playback is not evidence that a fresh request after expiry was authorized.

Patrick confirmed the foreground expiry test worked: after signing in, loading/playing media and keeping the tab in the foreground for six minutes, another WAV download succeeded and the displayed media-session expiresAt advanced. This is user-observed evidence of foreground session/cookie renewal and a fresh authenticated media request after the original five-minute token lifetime.
