.scratch/social-signup/issues/11-trial-conversion-copy.md:17:Specify a durable background import for trial conversions into independent account-owned copies. Patrick requires physically copied files, a source-conversion relationship, preservation of the original, account-level persistence of pending imports, and copying after a pending source finishes. A failed source must remain recorded as a failure. The user-journey decision defers import listings and cross-device UI discoverability until conversion history ships; preserve the currently open eligible conversion through signup/sign-in. These requirements are settled; resolve the remaining lifecycle and technical boundaries.
.scratch/social-signup/issues/11-trial-conversion-copy.md:19:Define copy identity and idempotency, retry and partial-file cleanup, which metadata/files and available exports form the snapshot, and behavior when source exports finish later. Separate a source conversion failure from a copy failure, and publish a ready account copy only after its required files are available. Decide the persistent processing mechanism and recovery after interruptions without rerunning narration.
.scratch/social-signup/issues/11-trial-conversion-copy.md:27:Patrick confirmed stable destination conversion IDs allocated when imports are recorded; retries and repeated sign-ins resume the same import. Retry temporary copy failures automatically with increasing delays and a bounded budget; exhausted retries retain a retryable failed import, without rerunning narration or spending credits. The current conversion page may expose Retry copy. Preserve access to the original trial result while copying or after copy failure; Patrick explicitly leaves the exact UX transition unsettled. Do not assume an automatic seamless player switch has been approved. Publish the private copy only after required playback files are complete; partial files remain private and may be reused after verification, with cleanup after abandonment or final account deletion.
.scratch/social-signup/issues/11-trial-conversion-copy.md:29:Patrick confirmed snapshot semantics and independent export generation. Copy canonical audiobook data and audio segments required to generate exports independently, plus exports present in the captured snapshot. Missing exports may be generated from the account copy on demand without rerunning narration or spending credits. Later source changes or exports do not automatically propagate; preserve the source relationship for explicitly designed future operations.
.scratch/social-signup/issues/11-trial-conversion-copy.md:31:Patrick set the automatic retry window to eight hours from the first copy attempt; waiting for the source to finish does not consume that window. After exhaustion, retain a retryable failed import. Abandoned partial-file cleanup is manual rather than automatically scheduled after seven days; preserve the import record and destination conversion ID so a later retry remains possible. Final account deletion still requires cleanup of all account-owned files under the agreed deletion policy. Record source failure separately as Original conversion failed; do not rerun narration automatically or offer Retry copy without a finished source. Starting a new conversion follows normal allowance rules.
.scratch/social-signup/issues/11-trial-conversion-copy.md:33:Patrick confirmed that manual retry starts a new eight-hour window using the same destination conversion ID and verified reusable files. Repeated clicks during an active execution neither duplicate work nor extend the deadline. Freeze the source snapshot when copying first begins after source readiness, and retain that same snapshot across automatic and manual retries. The exact player transition is delegated to the authenticated-media proof; original access remains required and an automatic mid-playback switch is not assumed.
.scratch/social-signup/issues/11-trial-conversion-copy.md:39:Use a dedicated Cloudflare Workflow for each import execution, backed by Cup’s persistent import record. Allocate the destination conversion ID when recording the import, deduplicate by source conversion and destination account, and retain the same destination ID across repeated sign-ins and retries. Persist dispatch intent alongside the import and reconcile missed launches so execution continues independently of the client. Cup state remains authoritative rather than relying on retained Workflow history.
.scratch/social-signup/issues/11-trial-conversion-copy.md:41:Wait for authoritative source readiness, with durable rechecks to recover missed completion notifications. Record source failure separately as Original conversion failed; do not rerun narration or offer copy retry without a finished source. Starting another conversion follows normal allowance rules.
.scratch/social-signup/issues/11-trial-conversion-copy.md:45:Record the source metadata and intended file set when copying first begins after source readiness. Under the subsequent rollout simplification, copy finished source files as they exist without per-file version/checksum tracking; exact source-byte snapshot preservation across retries is not guaranteed. Ready source files remain unchanged during normal operation. Missing required files fail copying, while temporary errors receive normal retries. Manual modification during copying can produce an inconsistent result; stronger guarantees are deferred until editing is introduced. Physically copy canonical audiobook data, audio segments and other required playback files, and exports present in the snapshot; rewrite destination artifact references appropriately. Missing exports can be generated independently from the account copy without narration or credit consumption. Later source changes do not propagate. Preserve sourceConversionId and leave the original untouched.
.scratch/social-signup/issues/11-trial-conversion-copy.md:51:Automatically retry temporary failures with increasing delays for eight hours from the execution’s first copy attempt. Source waiting does not consume this window. Persist the absolute deadline; start no further automatic attempts after it. Retain a retryable failed import after exhaustion. Manual retry starts a fresh eight-hour execution window with the same destination ID and snapshot. Repeated clicks while active neither duplicate execution nor extend the deadline. Use execution generations and conditional state transitions to prevent outdated jobs from publishing. No copy retry spends credits.
.scratch/social-signup/issues/11-trial-conversion-copy.md:57:Preserve access to the original trial result while the source or copy is pending and after copy failure. The current conversion page can offer Retry copy for copy failures. The [authenticated-media proof](14-authenticated-media-proof.md) owns the exact transition to the private copy; an automatic mid-playback switch is not assumed. All history listings remain deferred.
.scratch/social-signup/spec.md:25:Reliable screen-locked Android playback remains the desired outcome. Patrick chose to retain the HTML player and first measure one realistically sized MP3 before deciding whether native playback is necessary. The native experiment is paused; no replacement player is selected. Preserve the tested resume-refresh behavior, owner checks and five-minute JWT policy. Document observed limits and resolve any actual playback failures through the [media proof](issues/14-authenticated-media-proof.md).
.scratch/social-signup/spec.md:27:Ordinary logout targets only the current Supabase session, clears local credentials/private UI, and immediately stops playback. Successful server logout revokes refresh capability; offline/local clearing is not confirmed server revocation. Unexpected expiry first attempts refresh; if unsuccessful, pause and request sign-in while retaining playback position.
.scratch/social-signup/spec.md:44:| Anonymous private audiobook URL | Request sign-in without exposing title, source, status, or other details. |
.scratch/social-signup/spec.md:48:Account navigation exposes remaining allowance, the Google sign-in identity, logout, and account deletion. Adding another sign-in method is deferred. No history listing is introduced. Preserve the currently open eligible trial result through signup and copying; other imports are stored but not discoverable until history ships, including on other devices. The exact player transition is still a media-proof decision.
.scratch/social-signup/spec.md:50:Protect account conversion status, metadata, MP3, captions and exports, including range, HEAD, and conditional requests. No direct storage URL or shared cache may bypass authorization. Use private, no-store responses. A transferable signed URL alone is insufficient. Individual original trial audiobook links stay unlisted and accessible; remove shared trial-grant history listing access. Saved MP3/EPUB files outside Cup remain usable after logout/deletion; no DRM. Already-authorized responses may finish.
.scratch/social-signup/spec.md:89:The client generates and persists a private random per-conversion receipt before submission, alongside the idempotency key. Send it over HTTPS; Cup stores its hash with the accepted source conversion. Retries must match the original receipt and reuse the conversion. Keep receipts out of URLs and logs. Validate at the source owner before accepting an import into an authenticated destination. Evidence has no time-based expiry: keep the installation receipt and source-side hash while the original trial conversion exists. Clearing installation storage may lose the local receipt.
.scratch/social-signup/spec.md:91:Import eligible installation-started conversions on signup or returning-account sign-in. Shared trial credentials and opened audiobook URLs are not evidence. Conversions without tracked evidence are not automatically imported. Clearing browser storage/reinstalling can lose unclaimed eligibility. Receipts may be reused across destination accounts, with one import per source/destination pair.
.scratch/social-signup/spec.md:93:Allocate a stable destination conversion ID when the import is recorded. Preserve sourceConversionId, physically duplicate files, and leave the original untouched. Use a dedicated Cloudflare Workflow per execution. Poll source readiness durably every minute, without completion-notification machinery. Record source failure separately; do not retry copying an unfinished failed source or rerun narration automatically.
.scratch/social-signup/spec.md:95:Record source metadata and the intended file set at the first copy attempt after source readiness. Copy finished source files as they exist without per-file version/checksum tracking. Ready source files remain unchanged during normal operation; missing required files fail the copy and temporary errors receive normal retries. Accept possible inconsistency if source files are manually modified during copying. Exact byte preservation across retries is not guaranteed; revisit stronger guarantees when editing is introduced. name: domain-modeling
description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.
---

# Domain Modeling

Actively build and sharpen the project's domain model as you design. This is the *active* discipline: challenging terms, inventing edge-case scenarios, and writing the glossary and decisions down the moment they crystallise. (Merely *reading* `CONTEXT.md` for vocabulary is not this skill: that's a one-line habit any skill can do. This skill is for when you're changing the model, not just consuming it.)

## File structure

Most repos have a single context:

```
/
├── CONTEXT.md
├── docs/
│   └── adr/
│       ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md
│       └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md
└── src/
```

If a `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists at the root, the repo has multiple contexts. The map points to where each one lives:

```
/
├── CONTEXT-MAP.md
├── docs/
│   └── adr/                          ← system-wide decisions
├── src/
│   ├── ordering/
│   │   ├── CONTEXT.md
│   │   └── docs/adr/                 ← context-specific decisions
│   └── billing/
│       ├── CONTEXT.md
│       └── docs/adr/
```

Create files lazily: only when you have something to write. If no `CONTEXT.md` exists, create one when the first term is resolved. If no `docs/adr/` exists, create it when the first ADR is needed.

## During the session

### Challenge against the glossary

When the user uses a term that conflicts with the existing language in `CONTEXT.md`, call it out immediately. "Your glossary defines 'cancellation' as X, but you seem to mean Y. Which is it?"

### Sharpen fuzzy language

When the user uses vague or overloaded terms, propose a precise canonical term. "You're saying 'account': do you mean the Customer or the User? Those are different things."

### Discuss concrete scenarios

When domain relationships are being discussed, stress-test them with specific scenarios. Invent scenarios that probe edge cases and force the user to be precise about the boundaries between concepts.

### Cross-reference with code

When the user states how something works, check whether the code agrees. If you find a contradiction, surface it: "Your code cancels entire Orders, but you just said partial cancellation is possible. Which is right?"

### Update CONTEXT.md inline

When a term is resolved, update `CONTEXT.md` right there. Don't batch these up: capture them as they happen. Use the format in [CONTEXT-FORMAT.md](./CONTEXT-FORMAT.md).

`CONTEXT.md` should be totally devoid of implementation details. Do not treat `CONTEXT.md` as a spec, a scratch pad, or a repository for implementation decisions. It is a glossary and nothing else.

### Offer ADRs sparingly

Only offer to create an ADR when all three are true:

1. **Hard to reverse**: the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful
2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will wonder "why did they do it this way?"
3. **The result of a real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons

If any of the three is missing, skip the ADR. Use the format in [ADR-FORMAT.md](./ADR-FORMAT.md).
"}}}

Automate backend invariants and failure injection without live provider calls for every test. Run real-device authentication and media proofs on Android and web. Application implementation must follow the repository’s applicable validation commands; this draft has only Markdown/link validation.

## Gaps and contradictions requiring resolution

| Remaining work | Why it blocks readiness | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Provider setup and native proof | Terraform-created hosted project evwjipxgacwotgbmqtla has Google enabled. Android native login, secure persistence, expiry refresh, logout and local Worker verification pass; hosted web OAuth baseline passes. Web PKCE/session integration, local OSS setup and Google disconnect/lifecycle checks remain to be completed. Apple/iOS are deferred. | [Setup](issues/15-native-auth-setup.md), [native proof](issues/08-native-auth-proof.md) |
| Authenticated media and trial-copy transition | Web and Android prototype checks support owner-only cookie transport, MP3 playback, captions and downloads; Android resume authorization and the long-MP3 background observation passed. The exact transition from a currently open trial result to its account copy remains undecided. Fresh audio requests while locked after JWT expiry and recovery from a failed audio request remain unverified. | [Media proof](issues/14-authenticated-media-proof.md) |
| Resend onboarding and delivery proof | Resend account exists; cup-audio.com is verified in Ireland and Patrick reports RESEND_API_KEY stored on the Worker. A direct Resend API test was accepted and Patrick confirmed Gmail inbox delivery (not spam). Production Worker integration and retry/idempotency verification remain pending. Apple relay checks are deferred. | [Email setup](issues/19-email-setup.md) |
| Physical deletion verification | Completion and provider-outage policy are settled; specify handling of already-running writes and the final sweep/quiescence criterion. | [Rollout](issues/07-launch-and-specification.md) |
| Concrete storage/API contract | Pin tables, uniqueness/check constraints, state transitions, routing-registry reconciliation and existing schema/workflow compatibility. Preserve trial defaults, never publicize missing account records. | [Rollout](issues/07-launch-and-specification.md) |
| Operational bounds | Specify copy strategy/per-file size and timeout bounds, trusted IP identification and provisioning background retry/backoff policy. | [Rollout](issues/07-launch-and-specification.md) |
| Privacy of operational records | Sentry failure logs may include email; prefer fourteen-day retention and accept thirty days if unavailable. Setup must verify and record the actual policy, including avoiding longer-retained copies. Import evidence has no time-based expiry while its source exists. Completed-deletion receipts, including Cup/Supabase user identifiers, expire ninety days after deletion and notification processing finish. Specify expiry enforcement and remaining deletion-marker/notification-state handling; reconcile stale-token rejection with identity deletion and minimal retention. | [Rollout](issues/07-launch-and-specification.md) |

Superseded proposals were excluded: full data reset, imported-history UI, immediate live session checks on every request, no recovery period, 24-hour copy retries, automatic age-based partial cleanup, completion events for source readiness, staged rollout, emergency controls, Cloudflare email, and 24-hour email retries.

The draft is ready for review, not implementation handoff. Keep rollout and proof tickets open until these gaps have concrete answers and the required integration evidence exists.

## Question

Configure Resend for Cup <no-reply@cup-audio.com>, verify the sending domain, keep the sending API key server-side, and verify ordinary delivery, provider acceptance versus delivery outcomes, and idempotent retry within the twenty-three-hour window. Apple private-relay registration, Hide My Email delivery and Apple revocation sequencing are deferred. Use local fake delivery for ordinary automated tests and intentional real delivery tests only. Record configuration locations without secrets. Do not treat a checklist as successful provisioning. Coordinate the revocation sequence with the native proof; setup is not authorized to invent the unresolved deletion-completion policy.

Selected as the next unclaimed, unblocked ticket on the resumed wayfinder invocation. No Resend account or domain verification has been confirmed. Begin with Resend account access, then add cup-audio.com as a sending domain to preserve the agreed <no-reply@cup-audio.com> sender. Obtain the exact DNS records from that account; do not invent record values or replace existing receiving-mail records. Keep open/click tracking disabled for these transactional notifications. After verification, create a sending-only API key restricted to that domain and store it server-side as a secret. Do not paste credentials into the tracker or conversation. Apple relay registration and live delivery/revocation verification remain incomplete until the needed account access and explicit test recipient are available.

References: [Resend domain verification](https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/domains/introduction), [API-key permissions and domain restrictions](https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/api-keys/introduction). This is a setup plan, not completed provisioning.

API-key storage, actual sending/delivery tests, and Apple relay registration/revocation checks remain unverified; keep this ticket claimed.

Patrick confirmed completion of the API-key creation step. Secret value was not shared. Next store it as RESEND_API_KEY on the create-audiobook-from-url Worker using the interactive Wrangler secret prompt. Upload and delivery have not yet been confirmed.

Resend accepted it with HTTP 200 and email ID 01a0c873-f15b-705d-a2ec-fef1635138ed. Used idempotency key cup-setup-test-20260922-01. Use the agreed local Supabase CLI/Docker development approach; hosted production setup is separate. Real Google/Apple registrations remain prerequisites for native social-login validation. Google Cloud access has not been established. Patrick subsequently confirmed an existing Apple Developer Program membership; enrollment is not a prerequisite, but Cup’s Sign in with Apple configuration remains to be created. No services have been provisioned and no login flow has been validated.

Local readiness check: Docker daemon responds (29.8.0), Xcode developer directory is configured, no Android devices appear in adb devices, and Supabase CLI is not installed as a standalone command. Provider registrations remain absent as previously confirmed. Start with Google Cloud project/consent setup; Google local OAuth callback is <http://127.0.0.1:54321/auth/v1/callback> per its Supabase guide. Apple web callback hosting and device connectivity must be resolved before completing provider configuration. Sources: [Google setup](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/social-login/auth-google), [Apple setup](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/social-login/auth-apple).

Patrick currently lacks access to the Apple account holding the individual Developer Program membership and requested working on rollout planning meanwhile. Setup and native proof remain pending; do not infer membership or credentials are absent.

Patrick supplied the created hosted Supabase project URL: <https://oiehcntuiazvunyzngmi.supabase.co> (project reference oiehcntuiazvunyzngmi). Hosted Google OAuth callback: <https://oiehcntuiazvunyzngmi.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback>. Project region, provider configuration and authentication behavior have not been verified. Next prepare the Google Cloud project and Google Auth Platform consent/client configuration. Local OSS development remains the agreed development approach; this hosted project does not replace it.

CLI inspection confirmed gcloud is installed and authenticated as <patrick.kerschbaum@gmail.com>, and the existing cup-production project is ACTIVE. No duplicate project was created. The requested external Google Auth Platform branding/audience/test-user setup is not exposed by the inspected supported gcloud commands. IAP OAuth commands are deprecated and not a generic OAuth management API; IAM OAuth clients target Google Cloud resource access rather than this Sign in with Google registration. Continue those steps in Google Auth Platform console; no auth configuration was changed by this inspection. References: [IAP command limitations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/alpha/iap/oauth-clients), [Google console setup guidance](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/social-login/auth-google).

Terraform has now created the replacement hosted project evwjipxgacwotgbmqtla; use callback <https://evwjipxgacwotgbmqtla.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback> for subsequent Google configuration. Google web client credentials are absent from both checked local environment files. Prepared empty TF_VAR_google_web_client_id and TF_VAR_google_web_client_secret entries in ignored terraform/.env.local. Google client creation/update remains pending; no Google provider was enabled in Supabase. The existing Google Auth Platform Clients tab was visible, but Patrick was actively using the browser, so no further UI actions were taken. Configure a Web application client in cup-production with JavaScript origin <https://cup-audio.com> and the new hosted callback; local OSS callback <http://127.0.0.1:54321/auth/v1/callback> may be included for development. Google Web client credentials supplied in ignored terraform/.env.local. Terraform now manages external_google_enabled=true, the supplied web client ID/secret and external_google_skip_nonce_check=false. Initial apply failed with a connection reset; direct API read confirmed unchanged disabled state. A fresh plan and retry succeeded. Independent Management API verification confirms Google enabled, matching client ID, nonce checking enabled and jwt_exp=300. The public authorize endpoint returns HTTP 302 to accounts.google.com with the expected client ID and callback <https://evwjipxgacwotgbmqtla.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback>. Final full production plan reports no changes. This verifies configuration and flow initiation only, not Google callback acceptance, client-secret exchange, completed login or native authentication. Those proofs and native client registration remain pending.

Completed hosted Google web-login proof on 2026-09-22. Patrick completed Google consent and returned to Cup's app URL. Independent Supabase Admin API verification confirms a Google identity, confirmed email and last_sign_in_at 2026-09-22T14:04:10.191129Z. This proves the configured Google client, callback and authorization-code exchange produce a Supabase session. The test used the implicit callback flow; production application integration and native authentication are not proven. No callback tokens are recorded in this ticket. Production web integration should use PKCE and remove authentication callback parameters after processing.

Android debug signing certificate SHA-1 verified: A3:38:65:6D:37:74:87:30:B2:1F:17:29:F5:F4:27:08:91:BE:4B:90. Package com.cup_audio.app. Requested an Android OAuth client named Cup Android local debug in cup-production and a connected device or Google Play emulator. Found Java 21 at /opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@21 and SDK at ~/Library/Android/sdk; no installation needed. Prototype APK successfully built with that certificate. The Android OAuth client registration and runtime login have not yet been confirmed.

Patrick confirmed Android OAuth client creation: 1064540876713-kee7oq8f61ib7m24j2epg0c1qlpcsro7.apps.googleusercontent.com. Connected Pixel 10 Pro detected via ADB. Installed the prototype with adb install -r successfully and launched com.cup_audio.app/.MainActivity: Status ok, COLD launch, process running. The plugin continues to use the Web client ID as the Google token audience. Awaiting Patrick's observation of rendered UI and native login result; installation/launch alone do not prove authentication.

Pixel 10 Pro runtime setup is now confirmed: Patrick observed the rendered prototype and successful native Google login/Supabase exchange, refresh, logout/relogin with stable user ID, and cancellation. The Android debug registration is sufficient for this tested flow. Apple/iOS setup remains outstanding; this prerequisite ticket is not yet fully resolved.

+## Comments
+
+Starting a partial media proof after the core Android/web session checks passed. The broader auth ticket remains open for remaining Google lifecycle/local-development checks; this media work does not imply those are resolved. First test same-origin web cookie transport, then independently assess Android origin/cookie behavior.
+
+Prepared a first web-only cookie transport proof in the [isolated prototype](../../../apps/mobile-app/prototype-auth/README.md). A bearer-authenticated endpoint sets an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie containing the same short-lived JWT; the media route verifies it and a fixed prototype owner before serving a synthetic eight-minute WAV. Every response is private/no-store. Production must use Secure cookies and appropriate origin/path/CSRF design; the HTTP localhost cookie is only a proof. No public storage URL or token-bearing media URL is used. A foreground timer updates the cookie from the Supabase session every thirty seconds while this media proof is loaded; logout pauses/unloads audio and clears the cookie. This is not yet an agreed production transport.
+
+Local workerd tests pass for anonymous denial, non-owner 404, expired-token denial, authenticated byte ranges, invalid ranges, anonymous conditional-request denial, owner/anonymous HEAD and cookie issuance, alongside all twelve JWT tests. The fixture owner is Patrick's existing Supabase subject; tests sign ephemeral tokens with a separate fixture key. No new real account or private audio was created. Runtime browser playback/seeking/download/logout observations remain pending. Android cross-origin cookie behavior, background/expiry recovery, captions, MP3/EPUB, full conditional semantics and trial-copy player transition remain unproven. Current synthetic WAV proof does not resolve this ticket.
+
+Sources: [HTML media credential modes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLMediaElement/crossOrigin), [Capacitor native cookies](https://github.com/ionic-team/capacitor/blob/main/core/cookies.md). Cup currently uses an anonymous HTML audio element and direct download links; this proof investigates how those requests can carry owner credentials without a transferable signed media URL.
+
+Patrick confirmed all initial web media observations: the synthetic WAV played with the expected beeps, seeking forward/backward resumed playback, the authenticated WAV download succeeded, logout stopped playback, and another download attempt after logout failed. This validates the initial same-origin browser cookie transport and visible logout cleanup for this fixture. It does not yet prove renewal across access-token expiry, background recovery, Android transport, captions or MP3/EPUB behavior. In particular, buffered playback is not evidence that a fresh request after expiry was authorized.
+
+Patrick confirmed the foreground expiry test worked: after signing in, loading/playing media and keeping the tab in the foreground for six minutes, another WAV download succeeded and the displayed media-session expiresAt advanced. This is user-observed evidence of foreground session/cookie renewal and a fresh authenticated media request after the original five-minute token lifetime. It does not establish behavior while browser timers are suspended, Android cookie transport, or recovery from a failed refresh. The media proof remains claimed.
+
+On 2026-09-23 prepared the Android cross-origin media experiment: an additional local HTTPS Worker on port 8789, exact credentialed CORS for the Capacitor origin <https://localhost>, HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=None media cookies and a debug-only Android trust anchor for the locally generated certificate. TLS validation remains enabled, the private key stays in ignored host storage, and no Worker is deployed. Android UI uses WebView fetch with credentials and a credentialed audio element; this intentionally tests WebView cookie/media behavior rather than inferring it from CapacitorHttp. Logout pauses/unloads audio and clears the endpoint cookie. The download button verifies full WAV transfer, not saving to Android Downloads.
+
+APK build and the existing twenty-one Worker checks pass; a TLS-verified unauthenticated request to the new endpoint returns 401. Pixel is absent from ADB, so installation and device observations remain pending reconnection. Build success and host-side checks do not establish Android cookie acceptance, playback, seeking or download transfer. HTTPS setup references are in the prototype README.
+
+On 2026-09-23 the Pixel 10 Pro reconnected; the updated APK installed successfully, ADB forwarded ports 8789/8788, and the app cold-launched. Patrick confirmed all four Android media checks: credentialed audio played, seeking forward/backward resumed playback, full authenticated WAV transfer returned 200 with 7680044 bytes and passed, and logout stopped playback followed by a transfer returning 401. This establishes initial cross-origin WebView cookie transport with HTTPS and visible logout cleanup on the tested device. It does not establish Android Downloads saving, foreground renewal after expiry, background behavior, captions or MP3/EPUB compatibility. The broader media proof remains claimed.
+
+Patrick confirmed the Android foreground expiry test on 2026-09-23: after signing in, loading/playing private audio and keeping the app foregrounded with the screen awake for six minutes, authenticated download transfer still reported passed and the media expiresAt advanced. This is user-observed evidence of foreground Supabase session/media-cookie renewal and a fresh authenticated request after the original five-minute token expired. Android background/screen-lock behavior and recovery after suspended timers remain unproven, as do actual Downloads saving, MP3/EPUB and captions.
+
+Android background test failed: Patrick observed 401 for the first download transfer after locking the phone for six minutes. Whether playback continued throughout is unknown. Expired media authorization after suspended foreground renewal is the working explanation; no server-side expiry trace was captured for that request.
+
+Updated the prototype with Capacitor App 8.1.1 foreground-state handling. It stops the foreground timer in the background, renews session/media-cookie authorization on resume, shares concurrent renewal work, and makes authenticated transfer await renewal when media is loaded. Failed renewal pauses playback and reports retry/sign-in guidance. Logout disables renewal and drains outstanding renewal before clearing the cookie. A temporary Node harness exercising the actual module with mocked lifecycle/network boundaries passed resume plus immediate transfer ordering and logout during renewal; this checks coordination, not real Android behavior. APK build passes. The six-minute lock/unlock device retest is still required, and uninterrupted background playback remains unknown.
+
+Patrick confirmed the updated Android six-minute lock/unlock retest worked: after unlocking, an immediate authenticated transfer returned 200/passed without manually reloading audio. This validates post-resume authorization recovery on the tested Pixel, with transfer waiting for session/media-cookie renewal. The earlier post-unlock 401 is resolved for this tested path. Uninterrupted playback throughout screen lock and automatic recovery of a failed HTML audio resource remain unverified; transfer recovery does not establish either behavior.
+
+Extended the local proof with a synthetic thirty-second MP3, three timed WebVTT cues and a minimal EPUB 3 test book. Assets are embedded only in the authenticated Worker; owner authorization precedes format/range responses. Added web/native format players with a visible caption-text display driven by track cues. Android has a prototype-only MediaStore Downloads plugin for small authenticated MP3/EPUB files, using pending insertion then publication, without storage permissions on Android 10+. JavaScript fetches the authorized file before passing its bytes to the native saver; whole-file buffering/base64 is intentionally limited to these small fixtures and is not a large-audiobook download design.
+
+Existing Worker checks and additional MP3/VTT/EPUB owner/non-owner/anonymous checks plus MP3 range checks pass. ffprobe confirms thirty-second MP3 duration and unzip verifies EPUB archive integrity; EPUB-reader rendering remains unverified. Android APK builds successfully. Runtime format playback/captions, actual file saving/opening and denial after logout remain pending user observations. Existing external downloads should remain usable after logout by the agreed policy.
+
+Patrick confirmed the Android MP3/captions/EPUB checklist: MP3 playback and seeking worked, caption text changed at the expected intervals, both test files appeared in Downloads and the opening check was confirmed, logout cleared playback/captions and blocked new saves while previously saved files remained. The response did not separately identify browser observations, so the corresponding web format checks remain pending. These results validate the small-fixture Android path; they do not establish large-file streaming, uninterrupted background playback or the trial-copy transition.
+
+Patrick clarified that the same MP3/captions/EPUB checklist was also run successfully in the web prototype. Web MP3 playback/seeking, timed caption display, MP3/EPUB downloads/opening, logout clearing playback/captions and denial of new saves are therefore user-confirmed as well. Existing saved files remain usable. Both tested platforms now pass the small-fixture format/export checks; large-file transfer strategy, uninterrupted background playback, failed-player recovery and trial-copy transition remain unresolved.
+
+Added an Android background observer to the eight-minute WAV player: arm while playing, capture monotonic elapsed time and media position on background/return, and report pause/playing/waiting/stalled/ended/error/seeking events. The first bounded observation is ninety seconds, distinct from the five-minute authentication-expiry tests. Position progress and WebView-delivered events are evidence of player behavior, not guaranteed continuous audible output or fresh authorized network traffic. Buffered content and suspended event delivery limit the observation. Device results remain pending.
+
+Android recommends a native media playback service for reliable background playback; the current proof has no such service. Evaluate a native player and background credential-refresh ownership before committing to production background streaming. [Android Media3 guide](https://developer.android.com/media/implement/playback-app), [Capawesome Audio Player](https://capawesome.io/docs/sdks/capacitor/audio-player/). No paid plugin was acquired or production architecture selected. The observer APK builds successfully.
+
+Patrick reported the Android background observation: elapsedSeconds 256, playbackProgressSeconds 256, pausedOnReturn false (clarified after the initial value was mistyped). The player advanced in line with elapsed time and remained playing on return on this Pixel. No event-list result was supplied. This supports continued playback during the observed lock period but does not prove uninterrupted audible output, new authenticated requests while backgrounded, five-minute-expiry renewal, or behavior under memory pressure. The observation lasted less than the configured access-token lifetime, and buffered content may explain continued playback.
+
+Background streaming design boundary: inspection confirms the prototype clears its renewal timer when Android backgrounds the activity. Its only renewal paths are foreground timer, app resume and foreground user actions. Therefore it has no mechanism to refresh media credentials during a suspended WebView session; another long buffered-playback observation cannot establish fresh-request authorization after expiry. Expired-token rejection is already covered by Worker tests. No additional six-minute user test is requested for that unchanged mechanism.
+
+For reliable background streaming, the candidate design is a native media playback service with native-side session refresh and authenticated media requests, independent of the WebView timer. Refresh-token rotation must have one coordinated owner across native playback and the UI; independently refreshing copied tokens from both sides is not an acceptable shortcut. A generic native-player plugin does not itself prove Supabase refresh integration. Android's recommended MediaSessionService keeps playback separate from the activity: [official guide](https://developer.android.com/media/media3/session/background-playback). This is a proposed direction, not a selected or validated implementation. Product scope choice remains: include reliable background streaming in the current release, or explicitly defer that guarantee and retain tested foreground/resume behavior. No JWT lifetime extension or public/signed media URL is proposed.
+
+Patrick agreed to keep reliable screen-locked Android streaming in the current release and pursue native Android background playback with coordinated session refresh. This is a requirement and design direction, not a completed proof or selection of a specific plugin. The next prototype must demonstrate a fresh authenticated media request after access-token expiry while the screen remains locked, with playback and refresh independent of suspended WebView JavaScript. Native playback and the UI must share one coordinated refresh owner so rotation cannot race. Preserve five-minute JWTs, owner/lifecycle checks and logout cleanup. Also cover refresh failure with recoverable playback position. The successful HTML-player tests remain evidence for foreground/web transport, not fulfillment of this native background requirement.
+
+Prepared a native Media3 1.11.1 MediaSessionService prototype with a ten-minute playlist of thirty-second synthetic MP3 items and ten-second maximum target buffering. Native request resolution supplies the current bearer token, serializes refresh under one native lock and refreshes near expiry without WebView JavaScript. The local Android Worker applies the existing JWT/owner checks to native bearer requests. Transfer-start instrumentation counts accepted native requests while the screen is noninteractive after the original token expiry; the report also exposes refresh count, playback position and a sanitized failure field. This tests fresh media access rather than only buffered position progress.
+
+The bounded proof transfers refresh ownership to native: it drains/stops HTML-media renewal, makes other WebView controls inert and keeps Supabase automatic refresh disabled. Stop halts playback, waits for native refresh to finish and returns the latest tokens to Supabase secure storage without displaying them. Native-owned credentials are memory-only in this prototype; process-death recovery, seamless activity recreation, durable native credential custody, concurrent native/JS recovery and full logout/failure UX are not production-ready. Do not treat the temporary handoff as the final session architecture. APK build and existing Worker authorization/format tests pass; locked-expiry native runtime evidence remains pending. No production app or deployed Worker was changed.
+
+Native startup initially failed for Patrick even after sign-out/sign-in. Inspection found the bridge used PluginCall.getLong for expires_at; the installed Capacitor implementation accepts only Java Long, while the current epoch-second value is represented as Integer. Changed the expiry boundary to accept Number.longValue. A standalone Java check reproduced rejection of the integer by the old accessor logic and verified the corrected conversion for Integer and Long timestamps. Added safe startup-stage/error-code reporting and disabled duplicate Start clicks. APK rebuild passes; startup/device retest remains required. No successful native background proof is claimed from this fix alone.
+
+Patrick chose the simpler next step: pause the native-player experiment and measure the existing HTML player with one realistic long MP3 before deciding whether replacement is necessary. This supersedes treating native playback as an already-selected implementation direction; reliable background behavior remains the desired outcome, with limits to be documented from evidence. The earlier manual post-unlock download 401 did not demonstrate an audio-player request failing while locked.
+
+Prepared a single 45-minute synthetic mono MP3 at Cup's actual 24 kHz/128 kbps encoding (43,201,196 bytes). It is stored in local R2 emulation only, served with normal ranges and owner checks, without forced segments, reconnects or throttling. A bounded in-memory request report records timestamps, methods, ranges and statuses, never credentials. The dedicated HTML player has no background renewal; reading its request report after unlock renews authorization for the report without reloading audio. Native controls are hidden for this run and no native playback service was running before reinstall. Build, fixture metadata checks and a focused auth-before-storage/range/report harness pass. Device playback/request observations remain pending; fast USB/local networking remains a limitation of this experiment.
+
+Patrick's first long-MP3 observation showed 474 seconds elapsed and 360 seconds of playback progress, with no pause/error event reported on return. The server report showed two successful 206 audio requests before the original five-minute JWT expired and no later audio request; an earlier 401 came from an unauthenticated host check before the test. This run does not show an audio authorization failure. Response lengths do not prove the bytes were all transferred, and the progress gap does not identify its cause.
+
+Patrick then reported that the same HTML player played continuously through seven minutes of screen lock, unlocking and switching apps on the Pixel 10 Pro. Keep the HTML player as the current Android choice and pause the native Media3 experiment. The later successful observation supports this choice for the tested device and workflow; it does not prove every Android background condition, a fresh audio request after token expiry while locked, or recovery if a later range request receives 401. The tested resume authorization behavior remains required. The exact transition from a currently open trial result to its independent private copy remains a product decision before this ticket can resolve.

+Starting a partial media proof after the core Android/web session checks passed. The broader auth ticket remains open for remaining Google lifecycle/local-development checks; this media work does not imply those are resolved. First test same-origin web cookie transport, then independently assess Android origin/cookie behavior.
+
+Prepared a first web-only cookie transport proof in the [isolated prototype](../../../apps/mobile-app/prototype-auth/README.md). A bearer-authenticated endpoint sets an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie containing the same short-lived JWT; the media route verifies it and a fixed prototype owner before serving a synthetic eight-minute WAV. Every response is private/no-store. Production must use Secure cookies and appropriate origin/path/CSRF design; the HTTP localhost cookie is only a proof. No public storage URL or token-bearing media URL is used. A foreground timer updates the cookie from the Supabase session every thirty seconds while this media proof is loaded; logout pauses/unloads audio and clears the cookie. This is not yet an agreed production transport.
+
+Local workerd tests pass for anonymous denial, non-owner 404, expired-token denial, authenticated byte ranges, invalid ranges, anonymous conditional-request denial, owner/anonymous HEAD and cookie issuance, alongside all twelve JWT tests. The fixture owner is Patrick's existing Supabase subject; tests sign ephemeral tokens with a separate fixture key. No new real account or private audio was created. Runtime browser playback/seeking/download/logout observations remain pending. Android cross-origin cookie behavior, background/expiry recovery, captions, MP3/EPUB, full conditional semantics and trial-copy player transition remain unproven. Current synthetic WAV proof does not resolve this ticket.
+
+Sources: [HTML media credential modes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLMediaElement/crossOrigin), [Capacitor native cookies](https://github.com/ionic-team/capacitor/blob/main/core/cookies.md). Cup currently uses an anonymous HTML audio element and direct download links; this proof investigates how those requests can carry owner credentials without a transferable signed media URL.
+
+Patrick confirmed all initial web media observations: the synthetic WAV played with the expected beeps, seeking forward/backward resumed playback, the authenticated WAV download succeeded, logout stopped playback, and another download attempt after logout failed. This validates the initial same-origin browser cookie transport and visible logout cleanup for this fixture. It does not yet prove renewal across access-token expiry, background recovery, Android transport, captions or MP3/EPUB behavior. In particular, buffered playback is not evidence that a fresh request after expiry was authorized.
+
+Patrick confirmed the foreground expiry test worked: after signing in, loading/playing media and keeping the tab in the foreground for six minutes, another WAV download succeeded and the displayed media-session expiresAt advanced. This is user-observed evidence of foreground session/cookie renewal and a fresh authenticated media request after the original five-minute token lifetime. It does not establish behavior while browser timers are suspended, Android cookie transport, or recovery from a failed refresh. The media proof remains claimed.

TLS validation remains enabled, the private key stays in ignored host storage, and no Worker is deployed. Patrick confirmed all four Android media checks: credentialed audio played, seeking forward/backward resumed playback, full authenticated WAV transfer returned 200 with 7680044 bytes and passed, and logout stopped playback followed by a transfer returning 401. This establishes initial cross-origin WebView cookie transport with HTTPS and visible logout cleanup on the tested device. It does not establish Android Downloads saving, foreground renewal after expiry, background behavior, captions or MP3/EPUB compatibility. The broader media proof remains claimed.
+
+Patrick confirmed the Android foreground expiry test on 2026-09-23: after signing in, loading/playing private audio and keeping the app foregrounded with the screen awake for six minutes, authenticated download transfer still reported passed and the media expiresAt advanced. This is user-observed evidence of foreground Supabase session/media-cookie renewal and a fresh authenticated request after the original five-minute token expired. Android background/screen-lock behavior and recovery after suspended timers remain unproven, as do actual Downloads saving, MP3/EPUB and captions.

Expired media authorization after suspended foreground renewal is the working explanation; no server-side expiry trace was captured for that request.

It stops the foreground timer in the background, renews session/media-cookie authorization on resume, shares concurrent renewal work, and makes authenticated transfer await renewal when media is loaded. Failed renewal pauses playback and reports retry/sign-in guidance. Logout disables renewal and drains outstanding renewal before clearing the cookie. Patrick chose the simpler next step: pause the native-player experiment and measure the existing HTML player with one realistic long MP3 before deciding whether replacement is necessary. This supersedes treating native playback as an already-selected implementation direction; reliable background behavior remains the desired outcome, with limits to be documented from evidence. The earlier manual post-unlock download 401 did not demonstrate an audio-player request failing while locked.

Prepared a single 45-minute synthetic mono MP3 at Cup's actual 24 kHz/128 kbps encoding (43,201,196 bytes). It is stored in local R2 emulation only, served with normal ranges and owner checks, without forced segments, reconnects or throttling. A bounded in-memory request report records timestamps, methods, ranges and statuses, never credentials. The dedicated HTML player has no background renewal; reading its request report after unlock renews authorization for the report without reloading audio. Native controls are hidden for this run and no native playback service was running before reinstall. Build, fixture metadata checks and a focused auth-before-storage/range/report harness pass. Device playback/request observations remain pending; fast USB/local networking remains a limitation of this experiment.

Patrick's first long-MP3 observation showed 474 seconds elapsed and 360 seconds of playback progress, with no pause/error event reported on return. The server report showed two successful 206 audio requests before the original five-minute JWT expired and no later audio request; an earlier 401 came from an unauthenticated host check before the test. This run does not show an audio authorization failure. Response lengths do not prove the bytes were all transferred, and the progress gap does not identify its cause.

Patrick then reported that the same HTML player played continuously through seven minutes of screen lock, unlocking and switching apps on the Pixel 10 Pro. Keep the HTML player as the current Android choice and pause the native Media3 experiment. The later successful observation supports this choice for the tested device and workflow; it does not prove every Android background condition, a fresh audio request after token expiry while locked, or recovery if a later range request receives 401. The tested resume authorization behavior remains required. The exact transition from a currently open trial result to its independent private copy remains a product decision before this ticket can resolve.

| Incoming mobile shared URL | Prefill form and require Submit; use account, otherwise usable trial, otherwise authentication. |
| Anonymous private audiobook URL | Request sign-in without exposing title, source, status, or other details. |
| Signed-in non-owner private URL | Generic not-found/unavailable response without details. |
| Credits unavailable | Preserve input, distinguish reserved from spent credits, block new conversion; existing owned content remains accessible. |

Account navigation exposes remaining allowance, the Google sign-in identity, logout, and account deletion. Adding another sign-in method is deferred. No history listing is introduced. Preserve the currently open eligible trial result through signup and copying; other imports are stored but not discoverable until history ships, including on other devices. The exact player transition is still a media-proof decision.

Protect account conversion status, metadata, MP3, captions and exports, including range, HEAD, and conditional requests. No direct storage URL or shared cache may bypass authorization. Use private, no-store responses. A transferable signed URL alone is insufficient. Individual original trial audiobook links stay unlisted and accessible; remove shared trial-grant history listing access. Saved MP3/EPUB files outside Cup remain usable after logout/deletion; no DRM. Already-authorized responses may finish.

Sources: [journeys](issues/06-account-and-trial-journeys.md), [access policy](issues/05-access-and-trial-isolation.md).

Record source metadata and the intended file set at the first copy attempt after source readiness. Copy finished source files as they exist without per-file version/checksum tracking. Ready source files remain unchanged during normal operation; missing required files fail the copy and temporary errors receive normal retries. Accept possible inconsistency if source files are manually modified during copying. Exact byte preservation across retries is not guaranteed; revisit stronger guarantees when editing is introduced. Copy canonical metadata, audio segments, required playback artifacts and exports in the snapshot, rewriting destination references. Generate missing exports independently without narration/credit charges. Later source changes do not propagate. Required artifacts must be complete and verified before publishing the private copy.

Retry temporary failures for eight hours from the execution’s first copy attempt, excluding source waiting. Backoff begins at ten seconds, doubles to a five-minute cap, and includes jitter. Enforce an absolute deadline. On exhaustion retain a retryable failed import. Manual retry starts a new eight-hour window and execution generation using the same destination ID/snapshot; active repeated clicks neither duplicate work nor extend deadlines. Reuse only verified files.

Abandoned partial-file cleanup is manual, previews exact files, and refuses active-copy files. Retain the import record after cleanup. Final-account deletion still requires durable automatic cleanup, including late writes. The current trial result remains available during copying/failure; player transition and Retry copy presentation await the media proof.

Source: [copy lifecycle](issues/11-trial-conversion-copy.md).

Patrick chose a five-minute access JWT lifetime with local JWT verification plus Cup ownership checks, accepting residual access-token validity until expiry instead of a live Supabase session check on every private request. Successful current-session logout revokes refresh capability and removes the locally stored session; Cup must also stop playback and clear private UI and any application-managed credential copies. A copied or stolen access token remains usable until its original expiry, at most approximately five minutes after successful revocation; logout does not restart that clock. Failed/offline server logout cannot be described as confirmed refresh-token revocation. This supersedes the earlier preference for immediate server-side rejection. Source: [Supabase signout semantics](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/signout).

## Answer

Patrick confirmed the five-minute JWT policy and its residual-token risk. Account conversion status, metadata, audio, captions, and exports require a valid owner session. Verify the JWT signature and expected issuer, audience, and expiry locally, then enforce Cup ownership on every protected request, including range, HEAD, and conditional responses. Do not serve private content through an unauthenticated storage path or a shared cache that bypasses authorization; use private, no-store responses. A bare audiobook URL does not authorize access.

Anonymous visitors to private links see sign-in without audiobook details. Authenticated non-owners receive a generic not-found/unavailable response without title, source, or status. Ordinary logout targets only the current session, clears local credentials and private UI, and stops playback immediately. Successful server logout revokes refresh capability; copied access JWTs can still authorize requests until their original expiry. Use a five-minute JWT lifetime without a live session check on every content request. A request already authorized can finish; exported files remain usable. Failed/offline logout must not be represented as successful server revocation. On unexpected expiry, attempt refresh; if it fails, pause and request sign-in while preserving playback position.

Remove the trial-grant history listing API; possession of a shared grant never authorizes enumeration. Existing trial conversions retain individual unlisted-link access, and account imports remain separate private copies under the resolved ownership policy. General account history remains out of scope. Update the grant-session glossary to remove its history promise. Concrete rollout/migration details remain in the rollout ticket.

The policy is settled; credential delivery to HTML media and downloads across web and Capacitor still needs a [focused compatibility proof](14-authenticated-media-proof.md). That proof must honor the policy rather than weaken owner authorization.

If copying fails, the original remains available with **Retry copy**. The [specification](/Users/pkerschbaum/.codex/worktrees/3529/cup/.scratch/social-signup/spec.md) and [media proof](/Users/pkerschbaum/.codex/worktrees/3529/cup/.scratch/social-signup/issues/14-authenticated-media-proof.md) are updated, and Markdown validation passes.

❓ **Q3 — Returning later:** Copying may still be underway when the user leaves the app. I recommend restoring this **one current result page** on the same installation when they return, including its copy status or Open private copy action. That gives mobile users a way back without adding a conversion history view. Agreed?
